name: fin_accrued_interest
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
purpose: Accrued coupon interest between the last coupon date and settlement.
returns: `DOUBLE` = face x annual rate x year fraction(last coupon, settle); with `ACT/ACT ICMA` it is face x rate / frequency x (days accrued / days in period), with frequency inferred from the coupon period. Requires last coupon <= settle <= next coupon, otherwise `NULL`. Face defaults to 100 and day count to `ACT/365F`.
example: SELECT fin_accrued_interest(DATE '2026-04-01', DATE '2026-01-01', DATE '2026-07-01', 0.04, 100.0, 'ACT/365F') AS accrued;

name: fin_active_return
purpose: Annualized mean active return `avg(r - benchmark_r) * annualization`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_active_return(r, benchmark_r, 252) AS active_return FROM (VALUES (0.010, 0.008), (-0.020, -0.015), (0.015, 0.010), (0.004, 0.002)) t(r, benchmark_r);

name: fin_ad_line
purpose: Chaikin accumulation/distribution line `sum(((C - L) - (H - C)) / (H - L) * volume)`; bars with `high <= low` add 0 (TA-Lib `AD`).
returns: `DOUBLE`. Order-independent native aggregate (a sum): grouped calls need no `ORDER BY`, and a running window reproduces the TA-Lib AD series. Rows with a `NULL` input are skipped; a non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Compensated summation.
example: SELECT fin_ad_line(high, low, close, volume) AS ad_line FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close, close + 1.5 AS high, close - 0.5 AS low, 1000 + 10 * (i % 9) AS volume FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_adf
purpose: Augmented Dickey-Fuller unit-root test with a fixed lag order.
returns: `STRUCT(stat, pvalue, lags, nobs)` of DOUBLE. Regresses `dx_t` on `x_{t-1}`, `max_lag` lagged differences and the deterministic terms (`n` none, `c` constant, `ct` constant and trend); `stat` is the t-value of `x_{t-1}` and `pvalue` the MacKinnon (1994) approximation (statsmodels `adfuller(maxlag=max_lag, autolag=None)`). No automatic lag selection. Too few rows or a singular regression return `NULL`. Rows are ordered by `ts` (integer, DOUBLE, DATE, TIMESTAMP or TIMESTAMPTZ); ties on `ts` are ordered by value, so results never depend on row order or threads. Rows with a NULL argument are skipped; a NaN or infinite input makes the group `NULL`. 0.3.0 added `ts`. SQL macro.
example: SELECT fin_adf(x, ts, 1, 'c') AS adf FROM (SELECT i AS ts, sin(i * 1.7) + 0.3 * cos(i * 0.9) AS x FROM range(40) t(i));

name: fin_adosc
usage: fin_adosc(high, low, close, volume, 3, 10 ORDER BY ts)
purpose: Chaikin A/D oscillator `EMA(AD, fast) - EMA(AD, slow)` with `k = 2 / (period + 1)`, both EMAs seeded with the first AD value (TA-Lib `ADOSC`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `fast` (3) and `slow` (10), each 2..100000 (`fast > slow` flips the sign, as TA-Lib). First value at row `max(fast, slow) - 1`. 0.3.0 replaced an alias of the AD line and honors the periods. Recursive: depends on every row since the first row (or window frame start). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_adosc(high, low, close, volume, 3, 10 ORDER BY ts) AS adosc FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close, close + 1.5 AS high, close - 0.5 AS low, 1000 + 10 * (i % 9) AS volume FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_adx
usage: fin_adx(high, low, close, 14 ORDER BY ts)
purpose: Average directional index: Wilder average of DX, seeded with the mean of the first `period` DX values (TA-Lib `ADX`).
returns: `DOUBLE` in [0, 100]; positional `period` (14, 2..100000). First value at row `2 * period - 1`; undefined DX steps leave ADX unchanged (TA-Lib). 0.3.0 replaced `100 * avg(abs(H - L) / C)`. Recursive: depends on every row since the first row (or window frame start). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_adx(high, low, close, 14 ORDER BY ts) AS adx FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close, close + 1.5 AS high, close - 0.5 AS low FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_adxr
usage: fin_adxr(high, low, close, 14 ORDER BY ts)
purpose: ADX rating `(ADX + ADX period - 1 rows earlier) / 2` (TA-Lib `ADXR`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `period` (14, 2..100000). First value at row `3 * period - 2`. 0.3.0 replaced an alias of the old `fin_adx`. Recursive: depends on every row since the first row (or window frame start). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_adxr(high, low, close, 14 ORDER BY ts) AS adxr FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close, close + 1.5 AS high, close - 0.5 AS low FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_aggregate_return
purpose: Compound the returns of each group; alias of `fin_total_return`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; group by the period key to aggregate per period. 0.3.0 removed the ignored `period_key` parameter.
example: SELECT month, fin_aggregate_return(r, 'simple') AS monthly_return FROM (VALUES (1, 0.01), (1, 0.02), (2, -0.01), (2, 0.03)) t(month, r) GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;

name: fin_alpha
purpose: Annualized CAPM (Jensen) alpha `(avg(r - rf_p) - beta * avg(b - rf_p)) * annualization` over complete pairs.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. `risk_free` is annual; Rates are annual decimals converted geometrically to per-period rates, `(1 + rate)^(1/annualization) - 1`. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_alpha(r, benchmark_r, 0.02, 252) AS alpha FROM (VALUES (0.010, 0.008), (-0.020, -0.015), (0.015, 0.010), (0.004, 0.002)) t(r, benchmark_r);

name: fin_alpha_beta
purpose: Return CAPM alpha and beta together.
returns: `STRUCT(alpha DOUBLE, beta DOUBLE)`; same conventions as `fin_alpha` and `fin_beta`.
example: SELECT fin_alpha_beta(r, benchmark_r, 0.02, 252) AS capm FROM (VALUES (0.010, 0.008), (-0.020, -0.015), (0.015, 0.010), (0.004, 0.002)) t(r, benchmark_r);

name: fin_amihud_illiquidity
purpose: Amihud (2002) illiquidity `mean(abs(ret) / dollar_volume)` over rows with positive dollar volume.
returns: `DOUBLE` (unscaled; multiply by 1e6 for the usual reporting unit). The absolute value of `ret` is taken, so signed returns are accepted. Zero-dollar-volume rows are skipped; negative dollar volume or non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Order-independent native aggregate; runs over any window frame.
example: SELECT fin_amihud_illiquidity(ret, dollar_volume) AS illiquidity FROM (VALUES (0.010, 1.0e6), (-0.020, 2.5e6), (0.005, 0.8e6)) t(ret, dollar_volume);

name: fin_annual_return
purpose: Annualized compound return; alias of `fin_cagr`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; see `fin_cagr`.
example: SELECT fin_annual_return(r, 252) AS annual_return FROM (VALUES (0.001), (0.002), (-0.001), (0.0015)) t(r);

name: fin_annuity_payment
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
purpose: Level payment that amortizes a present value.
returns: `DOUBLE` with spreadsheet PMT signs (a positive loan gives a negative payment). Timing `end` (default) or `begin`; zero rates use the straight-line limit. Rates at or below -100% return `NULL`; unknown timing raises an error.
example: SELECT fin_annuity_payment(0.05 / 12, 360.0, 300000.0, 0.0, 'end') AS monthly_payment;

name: fin_anova_oneway
purpose: One-way ANOVA F test of equal group means.
returns: `STRUCT(f_stat, pvalue, df_between, df_within)` of DOUBLE; `F = (SSB / (k - 1)) / (SSW / (N - k))`, p-value from the F distribution (scipy `f_oneway`). `group` may be any type (hashed). NULL value or group rows are skipped; NaN/inf values make the result `NULL`. Fewer than two groups, `N <= k`, or zero within-group variance return `NULL`. SQL macro.
example: SELECT fin_anova_oneway(value, grp) AS anova FROM (VALUES (1.0, 'a'), (2.0, 'a'), (3.0, 'a'), (4.0, 'b'), (5.0, 'b'), (7.0, 'b')) t(value, grp);

name: fin_apo
purpose: Absolute price oscillator `MA(fast) - MA(slow)` (TA-Lib `APO`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `fast` (12), `slow` (26) and constant `ma_type` `'sma'` (default, as TA-Lib) or `'ema'` (SMA-seeded); swapped when slow < fast. First value at row `slow - 1`. Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_apo(close, 12, 26, 'ema' ORDER BY ts) AS apo FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_arithmetic_return
purpose: Arithmetic mean return `avg(r)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_arithmetic_return(r) AS mean_return FROM (VALUES (0.01), (-0.02), (0.015)) t(r);

name: fin_aroon
purpose: Aroon over the last `period + 1` rows: `aroon_up = 100 * (period - rows since the highest high) / period`, `aroon_down` likewise for the lowest low; ties pick the most recent extreme (TA-Lib `AROON`).
returns: `STRUCT(aroon_up DOUBLE, aroon_down DOUBLE, oscillator DOUBLE)` with `oscillator = aroon_up - aroon_down`; default period 14. First value at row `period`. 0.3.0 replaced the constant placeholder. Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_aroon(high, low, 14 ORDER BY ts) AS aroon FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 101 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS high, 99 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS low FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_aroonosc
purpose: Aroon oscillator `aroon_up - aroon_down` (TA-Lib `AROONOSC`).
returns: `DOUBLE` in [-100, 100]; default period 14. First value at row `period`. 0.3.0 replaced the constant placeholder. Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_aroonosc(high, low, 14 ORDER BY ts) AS aroon_oscillator FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 101 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS high, 99 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS low FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_asian_geometric_price
purpose: Price a continuously monitored geometric-average Asian option in closed form (Kemna-Vorst 1990).
returns: `DOUBLE`; Black-Scholes on the geometric average with volatility `vol / sqrt(3)` and drift `(r - q - vol^2 / 6) / 2`, discounted at `rate`. Also accepts an option spec. Invalid inputs return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_asian_geometric_price('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2) AS price;

name: fin_asset_or_nothing_price
purpose: Price an asset-or-nothing option.
returns: `DOUBLE` = S exp(-qT) N(+/-d1); at expiry returns spot when in the money and 0 otherwise. Also accepts an option spec.
example: SELECT fin_asset_or_nothing_price('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2) AS price;

name: fin_atr
usage: fin_atr(high, low, close, 14 ORDER BY ts)
purpose: Average true range: Wilder average of the true range, seeded with the mean of the first `period` true ranges (TA-Lib `ATR`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `period` (14, 1..100000). First value at row `period`. 0.3.0 replaced the mean of `high - low` and honors `period`. Recursive: depends on every row since the first row (or window frame start). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_atr(high, low, close, 14 ORDER BY ts) AS atr FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close, close + 1.5 AS high, close - 0.5 AS low FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_autocorr
purpose: Lag autocorrelation of a series ordered by `ts`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; Pearson correlation of `(x_t, x_{t-lag})` over overlapping pairs (pandas `Series.autocorr`), with `lag` counted in rows after ordering. Rows are ordered by `ts` (integer, DOUBLE, DATE, TIMESTAMP or TIMESTAMPTZ); ties on `ts` are ordered by value, so results never depend on row order or threads. Rows with a NULL argument are skipped; a NaN or infinite input makes the group `NULL`. 0.3.0 added `ts`. SQL macro.
example: SELECT fin_autocorr(x, ts, 1) AS lag1_autocorr FROM (SELECT i AS ts, sin(i / 3) AS x FROM range(30) t(i));

name: fin_avg_drawdown
purpose: Mean of the drawdown series `NAV_t / peak_t - 1` over all ordered observations.
returns: `DOUBLE` <= 0. Optional second argument `initial_nav` (positive) is accepted; drawdowns are scale-invariant so it does not change results. Returns below -1 or non-finite returns make the group `NULL`. Order-dependent native aggregate: pass `ORDER BY` inside the call or use a window `ORDER BY`; rows with equal ordering keys have unspecified relative order, so break ties in the key. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_avg_drawdown(r ORDER BY ts) AS avg_drawdown FROM (VALUES (1, 0.05), (2, -0.10), (3, 0.02), (4, -0.03), (5, 0.08)) t(ts, r);

name: fin_avg_price
purpose: Average price `(open + high + low + close) / 4` (TA-Lib `AVGPRICE`).
returns: `DOUBLE` scalar; `NULL` input or non-finite result gives `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_avg_price(100.0, 102.0, 99.0, 101.0) AS avg_price;

name: fin_bachelier_greeks
purpose: Compute Greeks under the normal forward-price model.
returns: `STRUCT(delta, gamma, vega, theta, rho)`; any NULL input, invalid domain, or non-finite output returns a NULL struct.
example: SELECT fin_bachelier_greeks('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 5.0) AS greeks;

name: fin_bachelier_implied_vol
purpose: Solve normal volatility in forward-price units per square root year.
returns: `DOUBLE`; omitted guess uses the quote's price, discount factor, and time scale rather than fixed price units. Optional explicit guess and absolute price tolerance (default `1e-8`). Uses bracketed Newton steps with bisection fallback and cached pricing terms. Requires positive time; expands the bracket for large normal volatilities. Returns zero at intrinsic within tolerance, or `NULL` on invalid inputs or failure to converge.
example: SELECT fin_bachelier_implied_vol('call', 1.9, 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05) AS normal_vol;

name: fin_bachelier_price
purpose: Price a European option under the Bachelier normal model on a forward: `exp(-rT) ((F - K) N(d) + vol sqrt(T) phi(d))` for a call, `d = (F - K) / (vol sqrt(T))`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `vol` is the normal (absolute) volatility in forward-price units per square-root year. Invalid inputs return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_bachelier_price('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 5.0) AS price;

name: fin_bar_spec
purpose: Pack a bar-sampling configuration (`tick`, `volume`, `dollar` or `imbalance` kind with a positive threshold) into a spec struct.
returns: `STRUCT(kind VARCHAR, threshold DOUBLE, price_col VARCHAR, volume_col VARCHAR)`; `kind` is `tick`, `volume`, `dollar` or `imbalance`, and `threshold` must be positive and finite, otherwise an error is raised.
example: SELECT fin_bar_spec('volume', 1000.0) AS spec;

name: fin_barrier_price
purpose: Price a continuously monitored European single-barrier option with an optional rebate.
returns: Reiner-Rubinstein `DOUBLE`; kinds are `down-in`, `down-out`, `up-in`, and `up-out`; inputs after barrier are `[rebate,] ttm, rate, vol[, dividend_yield]`.
example: SELECT fin_barrier_price('call', 'up-out', 100.0, 100.0, 120.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.0) AS price;

name: fin_bbands
purpose: Bollinger Bands: `middle = SMA(period)`, `upper`/`lower = middle +/- k * stddev` of the last `period` values (TA-Lib `BBANDS` with SMA and nbdevup = nbdevdn = `k`).
returns: `STRUCT(lower, middle, upper, width, percent_b)` of `DOUBLE`; positional `period` (20), `k` (2.0) and `ddof` (0 = population stddev as TA-Lib, 1 = sample; must be smaller than `period`). `width = (upper - lower) / middle` and `percent_b = (close - lower) / (upper - lower)` are `NULL` when their denominator is 0. `NULL` struct for the first `period - 1` rows. 0.3.0 changed the default from sample to population stddev and made `period` effective. Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_bbands(close, 20, 2.0, 0 ORDER BY ts) AS bands FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_beta
purpose: OLS slope `cov(r, b) / var(b)` over complete pairs.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `NULL` for fewer than two pairs or constant benchmark. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_beta(r, benchmark_r) AS beta FROM (VALUES (0.010, 0.008), (-0.020, -0.015), (0.015, 0.010), (0.004, 0.002)) t(r, benchmark_r);

name: fin_binomial_price
purpose: Price European or American options with CRR or Jarrow-Rudd trees.
returns: Defaults: dividend yield 0, 200 steps, European exercise, CRR tree. Steps accept `BIGINT` and must be between 1 and 100000 (otherwise an error). European prices use a linear-time terminal distribution; American prices use backward induction where early exercise matters. Zero volatility follows the discounted deterministic path. Bermudan exercise and unknown trees raise an error.
example: SELECT fin_binomial_price('put', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.0, 200, 'american', 'crr') AS price;

name: fin_bipower_variation
purpose: Estimate annualized bipower variation `pi/2 * sum(abs(r_t) * abs(r_{t-1})) * annualization / (n - 1)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; optional positional annualization (default 252). Returns `NULL` with fewer than two non-`NULL` returns. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Order-dependent native aggregate: pass `ORDER BY` inside the call or use a window `ORDER BY`; rows with equal ordering keys have unspecified relative order, so break ties in the key. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`.
example: SELECT fin_bipower_variation(log_r, 252 ORDER BY ts) AS bipower_variation FROM (VALUES (1, 0.001), (2, -0.002), (3, 0.0015), (4, -0.0005)) t(ts, log_r);

name: fin_black76_greeks
purpose: Compute Greeks under the lognormal forward-price model.
returns: `STRUCT(delta, gamma, vega, theta, rho)`; any NULL input, invalid domain, or non-finite output returns a NULL struct.
example: SELECT fin_black76_greeks('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2) AS greeks;

name: fin_black76_implied_vol
purpose: Solve annualized decimal Black-76 volatility.
returns: `DOUBLE`; defaults to guess 0.2 and absolute price tolerance `1e-8`. Uses bracketed Newton steps with bisection fallback and cached pricing terms. Requires positive time and price below the no-arbitrage upper bound. Returns zero at intrinsic within tolerance, or `NULL` on invalid inputs or failure to converge.
example: SELECT fin_black76_implied_vol('call', 7.58, 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05) AS vol;

name: fin_black76_price
purpose: Price a European option on a forward with Black-76: `exp(-rT) (F N(d1) - K N(d2))` for a call.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `d1 = (ln(F / K) + vol^2 T / 2) / (vol sqrt(T))`, `d2 = d1 - vol sqrt(T)`; annual decimal rate and volatility. Invalid inputs return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_black76_price('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2) AS price;

name: fin_black_litterman_returns
usage: fin_black_litterman_returns(market_weights, cov_matrix, views_p, views_q, tau := 0.05, omega := NULL, risk_aversion := 2.5)
purpose: Black-Litterman posterior expected returns.
returns: `LIST(DOUBLE)`; equilibrium `pi = risk_aversion * S w_mkt`, posterior `pi + tau S P' (P tau S P' + Omega)^-1 (Q - P pi)` (He and Litterman 1999). `views_p` is k x n, `views_q` has k entries; `omega` (k x k) defaults to `diag(P tau S P')`. Returns are in the covariance's periodicity. Shape mismatches, non-finite inputs or a singular view system return `NULL`; non-positive `tau` or `risk_aversion` raise an error. 0.3.0 added `risk_aversion`.
example: SELECT fin_black_litterman_returns([0.6, 0.4], [[0.04, 0.006], [0.006, 0.09]], [[1.0, -1.0]], [0.02], 0.05, NULL, 2.5) AS posterior_returns;

name: fin_bond_convexity
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
purpose: Convexity `(1 / P) d^2P / dy^2` in years squared of a regular fixed-coupon bond priced at nominal annual yield `ytm`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; defaults to frequency 2 and face 100. Geometric moments require logarithmic rather than linear work in coupon periods.
example: SELECT fin_bond_convexity(0.05, 0.04, 5.0, 2, 100.0) AS convexity;

name: fin_bond_duration
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
purpose: Macaulay duration in years (default) or modified duration `D_mac / (1 + ytm / frequency)` of a regular fixed-coupon bond.
returns: `DOUBLE`; defaults to frequency 2, face 100, and Macaulay duration in years. Specify `modified` for the first-order yield sensitivity. Uses logarithmic-time geometric moments. Unknown kinds raise an error.
example: SELECT fin_bond_duration(0.05, 0.04, 5.0, 2, 100.0, 'modified') AS modified_duration;

name: fin_bond_price
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
purpose: Discount a regular coupon bond using nominal annual YTM.
returns: `DOUBLE`; coupon periods are rounded from maturity times frequency. Uses a constant-time geometric sum, including zero and small yields. Invalid inputs or out-of-range period counts return `NULL`. No settlement or stub-period model.
example: SELECT fin_bond_price(0.05, 0.04, 5.0, 2, 100.0) AS price;

name: fin_bond_ytm
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
purpose: Solve nominal annual yield for the regular coupon model.
returns: `DOUBLE`; requires positive price and non-negative coupon. Safeguarded Newton inside a bracket above -frequency, including yields above 100; returns `NULL` if it cannot bracket or converge. `frequency` accepts `BIGINT`.
example: SELECT fin_bond_ytm(104.49, 0.05, 5.0, 2, 100.0) AS ytm;

name: fin_bootstrap_curve
purpose: Bootstrap a single discount curve from deposit, FRA, par swap, and zero-rate quotes.
returns: Table with `instrument`, `instrument_type`, `maturity`, `rate`, `discount_factor`, `zero_rate`, `forward_rate`, ordered by maturity. Arguments: table, instrument-type column, maturity column (year fraction), quoted-rate column, optional compounding for `zero` quotes and the output rates (`continuous` default, `simple`, `periodic`/`annual`, `semiannual`, `quarterly`, `monthly`, `daily`). Instrument types (case-insensitive): `deposit` simple money-market rate, DF(T) = 1 / (1 + rT); `fra` simple forward from `start_col` to maturity, DF(T) = DF(start) / (1 + f(T - start)), and the start must already be covered by the curve; `swap` par rate with a fixed leg paying every 1 / `fixed_frequency` years backward from maturity (named BIGINT `fixed_frequency`, default 1, between 1 and 365; a short first period when the maturity is not a whole number of periods), DF(T) solved so the fixed leg prices at par; `zero` zero rate in the requested compounding. Discount factors are interpolated log-linearly between nodes, starting from (0, 1), as in QuantLib's PiecewiseLogLinearDiscount; day counts are the caller's year fractions and there is no calendar or settlement lag. `zero_rate` is the rate from 0 to the maturity and `forward_rate` the rate from the previous node, both in the requested compounding. Optional named `instrument_col` (echoed as `instrument`, else NULL) and `start_col` (FRA start, year fraction). Rows are sorted by maturity, so input order does not matter. Unknown instrument types or compounding, NULL type/maturity/rate, non-positive or non-finite maturities, non-finite rates, duplicate maturities, a missing or invalid FRA start, swaps with more than 100000 fixed-leg payments, and quotes that imply a non-positive discount factor raise an error that names the function. An empty input returns no rows. Every `table_name` argument accepts a table, view, or CTE name, or a parenthesized query such as `'(FROM read_parquet(''t.parquet''))'`.
example: WITH quotes AS (SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('deposit', 0.25, 0.040, NULL), ('fra', 0.75, 0.042, 0.25), ('swap', 2.0, 0.045, NULL)) t(kind, maturity, rate, start_time)) SELECT * FROM fin_bootstrap_curve('quotes', 'kind', 'maturity', 'rate', 'continuous', start_col := 'start_time', fixed_frequency := 2);

name: fin_bop
purpose: Balance of power `(close - open) / (high - low)` per bar (TA-Lib `BOP`).
returns: `DOUBLE` scalar; 0 when `high <= low` (TA-Lib). 0.3.0 BREAKING: a per-row scalar instead of an aggregate average; smooth it explicitly, for example `avg(fin_bop(open, high, low, close)) OVER (ORDER BY ts ROWS 13 PRECEDING)`.
example: SELECT fin_bop(100.0, 102.0, 99.0, 101.0) AS balance_of_power;

name: fin_bps
purpose: Convert a decimal rate to basis points: `x * 10000`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `fin_bps(0.0125)` is 125. `NULL` input gives `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_bps(0.0125) AS bps;

name: fin_bsm_all
purpose: Return Black-Scholes-Merton price, Greeks, d1/d2, intrinsic value, and time value from explicit inputs or an option spec.
returns: STRUCT with `price`, Greek fields, `d1`, `d2`, `intrinsic`, and `time_value`.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_all('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2) AS bsm;

name: fin_bsm_charm
purpose: Return Black-Scholes-Merton charm.
returns: `DOUBLE`, the calendar-time decay of delta, -dDelta/dT per year. Also accepts an option spec.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_charm('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2) AS charm;

name: fin_bsm_color
purpose: Return Black-Scholes-Merton color.
returns: `DOUBLE`, the calendar-time decay of gamma, -dGamma/dT per year, with the same sign convention as theta and charm. Also accepts an option spec.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_color('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2) AS color;

name: fin_bsm_d1
purpose: Black-Scholes-Merton `d1 = (ln(S / K) + (r - q + vol^2 / 2) T) / (vol sqrt(T))`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `(spot, strike, ttm, rate, vol[, dividend_yield])` without an option kind, or an option spec. `ttm <= 0` or non-positive inputs return `NULL`.

name: fin_bsm_d2
purpose: Black-Scholes-Merton `d2 = d1 - vol sqrt(T)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; same arguments as `fin_bsm_d1`. `ttm <= 0` or non-positive inputs return `NULL`.

name: fin_bsm_delta
purpose: Return Black-Scholes-Merton spot delta from explicit inputs or an option spec.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `exp(-qT) N(d1)` for calls and `exp(-qT) (N(d1) - 1)` for puts.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_delta('put', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2) AS delta;

name: fin_bsm_elasticity
purpose: Black-Scholes-Merton option elasticity (lambda) `delta * S / price`: the percentage option-price change per 1% spot move.
returns: `DOUBLE`; also accepts an option spec. A zero price or invalid inputs return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_elasticity('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2) AS elasticity;

name: fin_bsm_gamma
purpose: Return Black-Scholes-Merton gamma from explicit inputs or an option spec.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `exp(-qT) phi(d1) / (S vol sqrt(T))`, the same for calls and puts.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_gamma(100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.0) AS gamma;

name: fin_bsm_greeks
purpose: Return Black-Scholes-Merton delta, gamma, vega, theta, and rho from explicit inputs or an option spec.
returns: STRUCT with `delta`, `gamma`, `vega`, `theta`, and `rho`.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_greeks(fin_option_spec('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2)) AS greeks;

name: fin_bsm_implied_vol
purpose: Solve annualized decimal BSM volatility.
returns: `DOUBLE`; optional dividend yield, guess (default 0.2), absolute price tolerance (default 1e-8), and iteration limit (default 100, capped at 1000). The solver also stops when the volatility step is below 1e-14 relative, so very large notionals converge. Also accepts `(spec, price)`, using `spec.vol` as the guess. Returns zero at intrinsic within tolerance, or `NULL` for impossible prices, invalid inputs, or failure to converge.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_implied_vol('call', 10.4506, 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05) AS implied_vol;

name: fin_bsm_price
purpose: Price a Black-Scholes-Merton option from explicit inputs or an option spec; `ttm`, rate, volatility, and dividend yield are annual decimal values.
returns: `DOUBLE`; dividend yield defaults to 0. Invalid inputs return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_price('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.01) AS price;

name: fin_bsm_price_dates
purpose: Black-Scholes-Merton price with time to expiry taken from valuation and expiry dates: `ttm = fin_yearfrac(valuation_date, expiry_date, day_count)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; dividend yield defaults to 0 and day count to `ACT/365F`. Dates accept `DATE`, `TIMESTAMP` or `TIMESTAMPTZ`; expiry on the valuation date returns intrinsic value and expiry before it returns `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_price_dates('call', 100.0, 100.0, DATE '2026-01-02', DATE '2026-12-18', 0.05, 0.2) AS price;

name: fin_bsm_prob_itm
purpose: Risk-neutral probability of finishing in the money, N(d2).
returns: `DOUBLE`; at expiry or zero volatility returns 1 or 0 from forward moneyness (0.5 exactly at the money). Also accepts an option spec.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_prob_itm('call', 100.0, 110.0, 0.5, 0.05, 0.25) AS prob_itm;

name: fin_bsm_prob_touch
purpose: Risk-neutral probability that spot touches the strike level before expiry.
returns: `DOUBLE` from the reflection principle with drift r - q - vol^2/2; `call` watches a level above spot and `put` a level below. Returns 1 when spot has already crossed the level. Also accepts an option spec.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_prob_touch('call', 100.0, 110.0, 0.5, 0.05, 0.25) AS prob_touch;

name: fin_bsm_rho
purpose: Return Black-Scholes-Merton rho.
returns: `DOUBLE`; unit `raw` (default, per 1.00 of rate) or `market` (per 1 percentage point, raw / 100). Also accepts `(spec[, unit])`.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_rho('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.0, 'market') AS rho_per_point;

name: fin_bsm_speed
purpose: Black-Scholes-Merton speed `dGamma/dS = -Gamma / S * (d1 / (vol sqrt(T)) + 1)`.
returns: `DOUBLE` per unit spot; also accepts an option spec. Invalid inputs return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_speed('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2) AS speed;

name: fin_bsm_theta
purpose: Return Black-Scholes-Merton theta.
returns: `DOUBLE`, the calendar-time decay -dV/dT. Unit `year` (default), `day` (/365), or `trading_day` (/252). Also accepts `(spec[, unit])`. Unknown units raise an error.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_theta('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.0, 'day') AS theta_per_day;

name: fin_bsm_ultima
purpose: Black-Scholes-Merton ultima `dVomma/dvol = -Vega / vol^2 * (d1 d2 (1 - d1 d2) + d1^2 + d2^2)`.
returns: `DOUBLE` per unit volatility cubed (raw units); also accepts an option spec. Invalid inputs return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_ultima('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2) AS ultima;

name: fin_bsm_vanna
purpose: Black-Scholes-Merton vanna `dDelta/dvol = -exp(-qT) phi(d1) d2 / vol`.
returns: `DOUBLE` per unit volatility (raw units); also accepts an option spec. Invalid inputs return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_vanna('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2) AS vanna;

name: fin_bsm_vega
purpose: Return Black-Scholes-Merton vega from explicit inputs or an option spec.
returns: `DOUBLE`; unit `raw` (default, per 1.00 of volatility) or `market` (per 1 volatility point, raw / 100). Also accepts `(spec[, unit])`.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_vega('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.0, 'market') AS vega_per_point;

name: fin_bsm_vomma
purpose: Black-Scholes-Merton vomma (volga) `dVega/dvol = Vega d1 d2 / vol`.
returns: `DOUBLE` per unit volatility squared (raw units); also accepts an option spec. Invalid inputs return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_vomma('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2) AS vomma;

name: fin_bsm_zomma
purpose: Black-Scholes-Merton zomma `dGamma/dvol = Gamma (d1 d2 - 1) / vol`.
returns: `DOUBLE` per unit volatility (raw units); also accepts an option spec. Invalid inputs return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_bsm_zomma('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2) AS zomma;

name: fin_business_days_between
purpose: Count business days in the half-open date range.
returns: `BIGINT`; calendar defaults to `weekday`, `NYSE` excludes exchange holidays. Reversed ranges return the negated forward count.
example: SELECT fin_business_days_between(DATE '2026-12-21', DATE '2026-12-28', 'NYSE') AS business_days;

name: fin_cagr
purpose: Compound annual growth rate `exp(annualization / n * sum(log1p(r))) - 1`, computed in log space.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. A return of -1 gives -1; returns below -1, non-finite returns, or empty input give `NULL`. Long series no longer overflow.
example: SELECT fin_cagr(r, 12) AS cagr FROM (VALUES (0.01), (0.02), (-0.01), (0.015)) t(r);

name: fin_calendar
purpose: Return business-calendar dates for a calendar name and date range.
returns: Table with `calendar`, `date`, `is_business_day`, `is_regular_session`. NULL arguments raise an error. The start date defaults to today in the session time zone (`current_date` with ICU, UTC otherwise), not the host time zone; the end date defaults to the start date.
example: SELECT * FROM fin_calendar('NYSE', DATE '2026-12-23', DATE '2026-12-28');

name: fin_calendar_spec
usage: fin_calendar_spec(calendar := 'weekday', timezone := NULL, regular_open := NULL, regular_close := NULL)
purpose: Pack a trading calendar (`weekday` or `nyse`), time zone and regular session hours into a spec struct.
returns: `STRUCT(calendar VARCHAR, timezone VARCHAR, regular_open TIME, regular_close TIME)`; `calendar` is canonicalized to `weekday` or `nyse` (aliases `weekdays`, `monfri`, `xnys`); other calendars, or a close not after the open, raise an error.
example: SELECT fin_calendar_spec('NYSE', 'America/New_York', TIME '09:30:00', TIME '16:00:00') AS spec;

name: fin_calmar
purpose: Calmar ratio: `fin_cagr(r, annualization) / abs(fin_max_drawdown(r ORDER BY ts))`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. `ts` orders the drawdown path (0.3.0 added it; the order-less form was nondeterministic). `NULL` when there is no drawdown.
example: SELECT fin_calmar(r, ts, 252) AS calmar FROM (VALUES (1, 0.05), (2, -0.10), (3, 0.02), (4, -0.03), (5, 0.08)) t(ts, r);

name: fin_cashflow_spec
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
purpose: Pack a cash flow into a `STRUCT(amount DOUBLE, date DATE, currency VARCHAR)` with an upper-cased currency.
returns: `STRUCT(amount DOUBLE, date DATE, currency VARCHAR)`; currency is upper-cased.
example: SELECT fin_cashflow_spec(1000.0, DATE '2026-06-30', 'usd') AS cashflow;

name: fin_cci
usage: fin_cci(high, low, close, 20, 0.015 ORDER BY ts)
purpose: Commodity channel index `(TP - SMA(TP)) / (constant * mean absolute deviation of TP)` over the last `period` rows, `TP = (high + low + close) / 3` (TA-Lib `CCI`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `period` (20) and `constant` (0.015, positive). `NULL` for the first `period - 1` rows; zero deviation gives 0 (TA-Lib). 0.3.0 replaced the median absolute deviation with the mean absolute deviation. Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_cci(high, low, close, 20, 0.015 ORDER BY ts) AS cci FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close, close + 1.5 AS high, close - 0.5 AS low FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_cents_to_money
purpose: Convert integer minor units to an exact decimal amount: `cents / 10^scale`.
returns: `DECIMAL(38, scale)`, exact (no DOUBLE rounding). `scale` must be an integer in 0..9, otherwise an error is raised. Non-integer `cents` are rounded half away from zero by the DECIMAL cast.
example: SELECT fin_cents_to_money(12345, 2) AS amount;

name: fin_changes
purpose: Count how many times consecutive non-NULL values differ when ordered by `ts` (Prometheus `changes`).
returns: BIGINT; 0 for empty or single-row groups. NULL x or ts rows are skipped; equal `ts` values are ordered by x. Buffers the group's values.
example: SELECT fin_changes(x, ts) AS changes FROM (VALUES (1, 1.0), (2, 1.0), (3, 2.0), (4, 2.0), (5, 1.0)) t(ts, x);

name: fin_changes_to_grid
purpose: Flag whether each grid sample differs from the previous grid sample (1.0 changed, 0.0 unchanged).
returns: DOUBLE `value`; NULL for the first grid point or when either sample is NULL. Grid points are `start_ts + i * step` for every point not after `end_ts` (at most 10,000,000 points; month steps are anchored at `start_ts`). Each point samples the last observation at or before it via an ASOF join; rows with NULL timestamp or value are skipped, and duplicate timestamps keep the row with the largest `seq_col` (else the largest value). Optional named `asset_col := 'col'` builds one grid per asset (output keeps that column) and `seq_col := 'col'` breaks timestamp ties. Optional 7th/8th args: method (only `last`) and a non-negative staleness interval after which the sample is NULL. Invalid start/end/step/method/staleness raise an error. Every `table_name` argument accepts a table, view, or CTE name, or a parenthesized query such as `'(FROM read_parquet(''t.parquet''))'`.
example: WITH ticks AS (SELECT TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 09:30:00' + i * INTERVAL '20 seconds' AS ts, 100 + (i % 5) * 0.1 AS price, 100.0 + 50 * (i % 3) AS volume FROM range(12) t(i)) SELECT * FROM fin_changes_to_grid('ticks', 'ts', 'price', TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 09:30:00', TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 09:34:00', INTERVAL '1 minute');

name: fin_chi2_cdf
purpose: Evaluate the chi-square CDF.
returns: `DOUBLE` in [0, 1]; regularized lower incomplete gamma with relative accuracy near 1e-12 in both tails and at large degrees of freedom (validated against scipy). `x <= 0` returns 0; non-positive or non-finite `df` returns `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_chi2_cdf(11.0705, 5.0) AS p;

name: fin_chi2_inv
purpose: Invert the chi-square CDF.
returns: `DOUBLE`; safeguarded Newton on the log tail from a Wilson-Hilferty start. `p` must be in (0, 1); quantiles that underflow return 0. Invalid inputs return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_chi2_inv(0.95, 5.0) AS x;

name: fin_clip
purpose: Clamp a value to `[lower, upper]`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `lower > upper` returns `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_clip(12.0, 0.0, 10.0) AS clipped;

name: fin_cmo
purpose: Chande momentum oscillator `100 * (avg_gain - avg_loss) / (avg_gain + avg_loss)` with Wilder averages seeded like RSI (TA-Lib `CMO`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; default period 14. First value at row `period`. No price movement gives 0. Recursive: depends on every row since the first row (or window frame start). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_cmo(close, 14 ORDER BY ts) AS cmo FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_component_risk
purpose: Compute each weight's contribution to portfolio volatility.
returns: `LIST`; component i is weight i times (covariance times weights) i divided by portfolio volatility. Components sum to portfolio volatility; zero portfolio volatility returns `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_component_risk([0.7, 0.3], [[0.04, 0.006], [0.006, 0.09]]) AS component_vol;

name: fin_conditional_drawdown_at_risk
purpose: Conditional drawdown at risk (Chekhlov, Uryasev and Zabarankin 2005): mean of drawdown magnitudes `1 - NAV_t / peak_t` at or beyond `fin_drawdown_at_risk`.
returns: `DOUBLE` >= 0; confidence defaults to 0.95 and must be in (0, 1). Order-dependent native aggregate: pass `ORDER BY` inside the call or use a window `ORDER BY`; rows with equal ordering keys have unspecified relative order, so break ties in the key. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_conditional_drawdown_at_risk(r, 0.8 ORDER BY ts) AS cdar FROM (VALUES (1, 0.05), (2, -0.10), (3, 0.02), (4, -0.03), (5, 0.08)) t(ts, r);

name: fin_corr_matrix
purpose: Labelled correlation matrix from long-format returns.
returns: `STRUCT(labels VARCHAR[], matrix DOUBLE[][])`; labels are the distinct assets cast to VARCHAR in ascending order. Rows are paired by `ts`; each entry is the Pearson correlation over the `ts` values where both assets have a return (pairwise complete, pandas `DataFrame.corr`), so the matrix can be non-PSD (see `fin_nearest_psd`). Entries with fewer than two pairs or zero variance are `NULL`. A duplicate `(ts, asset)` or NaN/inf return makes the result `NULL`. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. 0.3.0 replaced the one-cell placeholder `(asset, r)` signature.

name: fin_cov_matrix
purpose: Labelled sample covariance matrix from long-format returns.
returns: `STRUCT(labels VARCHAR[], matrix DOUBLE[][])`; same pairing, ordering and NULL rules as `fin_corr_matrix`, with sample (n - 1) covariances over pairwise-complete dates (pandas `DataFrame.cov`). Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. 0.3.0 replaced the one-cell placeholder `(asset, r)` signature.

name: fin_cramers_v
purpose: Cramer's V association between two categorical columns.
returns: `DOUBLE` in [0, 1]. Uncorrected: `sqrt(chi2 / n / min(r - 1, c - 1))` without Yates correction (scipy `contingency.association(method='cramer')`). `bias_corrected` uses Bergsma (2013). Categories of any type are hashed; NULL rows are skipped. A single category on either side returns `NULL`. SQL macro.
example: SELECT fin_cramers_v(x, y, false) AS cramers_v FROM (VALUES ('a', 'u'), ('a', 'u'), ('b', 'v'), ('b', 'v'), ('a', 'v'), ('b', 'u'), ('a', 'u')) t(x, y);

name: fin_crosscorr
purpose: Lagged cross-correlation of two series ordered by `ts`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; Pearson correlation of `(x_t, y_{t-lag})` (pandas `x.corr(y.shift(lag))`); negative lags lead `y`. Rows need both values. Rows are ordered by `ts` (integer, DOUBLE, DATE, TIMESTAMP or TIMESTAMPTZ); ties on `ts` are ordered by value, so results never depend on row order or threads. Rows with a NULL argument are skipped; a NaN or infinite input makes the group `NULL`. 0.3.0 added `ts`. SQL macro.
example: SELECT fin_crosscorr(x, y, ts, 1) AS lagged_corr FROM (SELECT i AS ts, sin(i / 3) AS x, sin((i - 1) / 3) AS y FROM range(30) t(i));

name: fin_cum_return
purpose: Cumulative compounded return; alias of `fin_total_return`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; see `fin_total_return`.
example: SELECT fin_cum_return(r, 'simple') AS cumulative_return FROM (VALUES (0.01), (0.02), (-0.01)) t(r);

name: fin_curve_bootstrap
purpose: Alias of `fin_bootstrap_curve`.
returns: Same arguments, named parameters, output, and errors as `fin_bootstrap_curve`; errors name `fin_curve_bootstrap`.
example: WITH quotes AS (SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('deposit', 0.5, 0.040), ('swap', 1.0, 0.042), ('swap', 2.0, 0.045)) t(kind, maturity, rate)) SELECT * FROM fin_curve_bootstrap('quotes', 'kind', 'maturity', 'rate', fixed_frequency := 2);

name: fin_curve_discount_factor
purpose: Discount using linearly interpolated zero rates and continuous compounding.
returns: `DOUBLE`; finite values and strictly increasing maturities are required. Flat extrapolation uses the nearest endpoint rate. Negative target times return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_curve_discount_factor([0.5, 1.0, 2.0], [0.04, 0.045, 0.05], 1.5) AS discount_factor;

name: fin_curve_spec
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
usage: fin_curve_spec(maturities, values, value_type := 'zero_rate', interpolation := 'linear', compounding := 'continuous', day_count := 'ACT/365F')
purpose: Pack a zero-rate or discount-factor curve with validated value type, interpolation, compounding and day count into a spec struct.
returns: `STRUCT(maturities DOUBLE[], values DOUBLE[], value_type, interpolation, compounding, day_count)`. `value_type` is `zero_rate` or `discount_factor`; only `linear` interpolation is supported; compounding and day count are canonicalized. Unknown names raise an error starting with `fin_curve_spec:`. Use `fin_validate_curve_spec` for the numeric checks.
example: SELECT fin_curve_spec([0.5, 1.0, 2.0], [0.04, 0.045, 0.05], 'zero_rate', 'linear', 'continuous', 'ACT/365F') AS curve;

name: fin_curve_zero_rate
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
purpose: Linearly interpolate zero rates.
returns: `DOUBLE`; finite, strictly increasing maturities and finite values are required. Lists must be non-empty and equal length. Flat extrapolation uses the nearest endpoint. Large curves use binary lookup; constant curves are validated once per input chunk.
example: SELECT fin_curve_zero_rate([0.5, 1.0, 2.0], [0.04, 0.045, 0.05], 1.5) AS zero_rate;

name: fin_cvar
purpose: Conditional value at risk (expected shortfall) at the given confidence.
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional arguments `(r [, confidence [, method [, loss_positive]]])` with defaults 0.95, `'historical'`, `true`. `historical`: mean of returns at or below the linear-interpolation `1 - confidence` quantile (positions within 1e-9 of an order statistic snap to it). `parametric`: normal `mean - sd * phi(z) / (1 - confidence)` with sample sd. Other methods raise an error; confidence must be in (0, 1). Positive loss by default; pass `false` for the signed tail return. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.

name: fin_data_quality_report
purpose: Data-quality summary of a numeric column: row count, NULL count, finite count, min, max and z-score outlier count.
returns: `STRUCT(n BIGINT, nulls BIGINT, finite BIGINT, min DOUBLE, max DOUBLE, outliers BIGINT)`; SQL aggregate macro. `min` and `max` cover finite values only (NULL when there are none), so NaN and infinity show up in `n - nulls - finite`; `outliers` is `fin_outlier_count(x)` (threshold 3, non-finite values ignored).
example: SELECT fin_data_quality_report(x) AS report FROM (VALUES (1.0), (NULL), ('nan'::DOUBLE), (2.0)) t(x);

name: fin_delta
purpose: Last minus first non-NULL value when ordered by `ts`.
returns: DOUBLE; NULL for empty groups. Equal `ts` values are ordered by x (first takes the smallest, last the largest). `ts` may be an integer, floating-point, `DATE`, `TIMESTAMP` or `TIMESTAMPTZ` column; constant-size state.
example: SELECT fin_delta(x, ts) AS delta FROM (VALUES (1, 10.0), (2, 12.0), (3, 11.5)) t(ts, x);

name: fin_delta_to_grid
purpose: Difference between each grid sample and the previous grid sample.
returns: DOUBLE `value`; NULL for the first grid point. Grid points are `start_ts + i * step` for every point not after `end_ts` (at most 10,000,000 points; month steps are anchored at `start_ts`). Each point samples the last observation at or before it via an ASOF join; rows with NULL timestamp or value are skipped, and duplicate timestamps keep the row with the largest `seq_col` (else the largest value). Optional named `asset_col := 'col'` builds one grid per asset (output keeps that column) and `seq_col := 'col'` breaks timestamp ties. Optional 7th/8th args: method (only `last`) and a non-negative staleness interval after which the sample is NULL. Invalid start/end/step/method/staleness raise an error. Every `table_name` argument accepts a table, view, or CTE name, or a parenthesized query such as `'(FROM read_parquet(''t.parquet''))'`.
example: WITH ticks AS (SELECT TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 09:30:00' + i * INTERVAL '20 seconds' AS ts, 100 + (i % 5) * 0.1 AS price, 100.0 + 50 * (i % 3) AS volume FROM range(12) t(i)) SELECT * FROM fin_delta_to_grid('ticks', 'ts', 'price', TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 09:30:00', TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 09:34:00', INTERVAL '1 minute');

name: fin_dema
purpose: Double exponential moving average `2 * EMA - EMA(EMA)`; each EMA stage is seeded with the SMA of its first `period` inputs (TA-Lib `DEMA`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; default period 20. First value at row `2 * (period - 1)`. Recursive: depends on every row since the first row (or window frame start). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_dema(close, 20 ORDER BY ts) AS dema FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_digital_price
purpose: Price a cash-or-nothing digital option.
returns: `DOUBLE` = payout x exp(-rT) x N(+/-d2); payout defaults to 1. At expiry returns the payout when in the money and 0 otherwise. Also accepts `(spec[, payout])`.
example: SELECT fin_digital_price('call', 100.0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.0, 10.0) AS price;

name: fin_discount_factor
purpose: Discount factor for an annual decimal `rate` over `t` years under a compounding convention.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `continuous` (default) is `exp(-rate t)`, `simple` is `1 / (1 + rate t)`, periodic conventions are `(1 + rate / f)^(-f t)` with `f` from the convention name (`annual`, `semiannual`, `quarterly`, `monthly`) or the optional `frequency` for `periodic`. Rates at or below -100% per period return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_discount_factor(0.05, 2.0, 'semiannual', 2) AS discount_factor;

name: fin_dollar_bars
purpose: Aggregate trades into dollar bars that close once accumulated abs(price) * volume reaches the threshold.
returns: Rows are ordered by (`asset_col`, ts, `seq_col`, price, volume), so ties are deterministic; rows with NULL ts or price (or NULL volume for volume-based bars) are skipped. AFML reset-accumulator convention (Lopez de Prado 2018, ch. 2.3): the bar closes on the first row whose running total reaches the threshold (relative tolerance 1e-12) and the next bar restarts at zero, so overshoot does not carry over. Returns [asset_col,] `bar_id` (0-based per asset), `start_ts`, `end_ts`, `open`, `high`, `low`, `close`, `volume`, `vwap`, `ticks`; the last bar of each asset may be incomplete. Volume must be finite and non-negative and the threshold positive, else an error. Named `asset_col`, `seq_col`. Every `table_name` argument accepts a table, view, or CTE name, or a parenthesized query such as `'(FROM read_parquet(''t.parquet''))'`.
example: WITH ticks AS (SELECT TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 09:30:00' + i * INTERVAL '20 seconds' AS ts, 100 + (i % 5) * 0.1 AS price, 100.0 + 50 * (i % 3) AS volume FROM range(12) t(i)) SELECT * FROM fin_dollar_bars('ticks', 'ts', 'price', 'volume', 40000.0);

name: fin_donchian
purpose: Donchian channel over the last `period` rows: `upper` = highest high, `lower` = lowest low, `middle = (upper + lower) / 2`.
returns: `STRUCT(lower DOUBLE, middle DOUBLE, upper DOUBLE)`; default period 20. `NULL` for the first `period - 1` rows. 0.3.0 made `period` effective. Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_donchian(high, low, 20 ORDER BY ts) AS channel FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 101 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS high, 99 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS low FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_dot
purpose: Dot product of two lists.
returns: `DOUBLE` with compensated (Dot2) accumulation; empty or different-length lists return `NULL`.

name: fin_down_capture
purpose: Down-market capture `avg(r) FILTER (b < 0) / avg(b) FILTER (b < 0)` over complete pairs.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_down_capture(r, benchmark_r) AS down_capture FROM (VALUES (0.010, 0.008), (-0.020, -0.015), (0.015, 0.010), (-0.004, -0.006)) t(r, benchmark_r);

name: fin_downside_deviation
purpose: Annualized downside deviation `sqrt(mean(min(r - mar_p, 0)^2)) * sqrt(annualization)` over all observations.
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `(r [, mar [, annualization]])`. `mar` is annual; Rates are annual decimals converted geometrically to per-period rates, `(1 + rate)^(1/annualization) - 1`. 0.3.0 changed `mar` from per-period to annual. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_downside_deviation(r, 0.0, 252) AS downside_deviation FROM (VALUES (0.01), (-0.02), (0.015), (-0.005), (0.012)) t(r);

name: fin_drawdown
purpose: Current drawdown `NAV_n / peak_n - 1` at the last ordered observation.
returns: `DOUBLE` <= 0; optional positional `initial_nav` is validated but does not change results. Order-dependent native aggregate: pass `ORDER BY` inside the call or use a window `ORDER BY`; rows with equal ordering keys have unspecified relative order, so break ties in the key. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_drawdown(r ORDER BY ts) AS current_drawdown FROM (VALUES (1, 0.05), (2, -0.10), (3, 0.02)) t(ts, r);

name: fin_drawdown_at_risk
purpose: Drawdown at risk (Chekhlov et al. 2005): linear-interpolation confidence quantile of drawdown magnitudes `1 - NAV_t / peak_t`.
returns: `DOUBLE` >= 0; confidence defaults to 0.95 and must be in (0, 1). 0.3.0 computes it from the drawdown series rather than from returns. Order-dependent native aggregate: pass `ORDER BY` inside the call or use a window `ORDER BY`; rows with equal ordering keys have unspecified relative order, so break ties in the key. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_drawdown_at_risk(r, 0.8 ORDER BY ts) AS dar FROM (VALUES (1, 0.05), (2, -0.10), (3, 0.02), (4, -0.03), (5, 0.08)) t(ts, r);

name: fin_drawdown_duration
purpose: Longest run of consecutive observations below the running peak.
returns: `BIGINT`; optional positional `initial_nav` is validated only. Order-dependent native aggregate: pass `ORDER BY` inside the call or use a window `ORDER BY`; rows with equal ordering keys have unspecified relative order, so break ties in the key. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_drawdown_duration(r ORDER BY ts) AS longest_drawdown_rows FROM (VALUES (1, 0.05), (2, -0.10), (3, 0.02), (4, -0.03), (5, 0.20)) t(ts, r);

name: fin_dv01
purpose: Dollar value of one basis point: price change `P(ytm - 0.0001) - P(ytm)` of a regular coupon bond for a 1 bp fall in yield.
returns: `DOUBLE` in price units per `face` (default 100), positive for a long bond; frequency defaults to 2. Same inputs as `fin_bond_price`.

name: fin_dx
usage: fin_dx(high, low, close, 14 ORDER BY ts)
purpose: Directional movement index `100 * abs(+DI - -DI) / (+DI + -DI)` (TA-Lib `DX`).
returns: `DOUBLE` in [0, 100]; positional `period` (14, 2..100000). First value at row `period`. When it is undefined (zero true range or DI sum) it keeps its previous value, 0 at first (TA-Lib). 0.3.0 replaced an alias of the old `fin_adx`. Recursive: depends on every row since the first row (or window frame start). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_dx(high, low, close, 14 ORDER BY ts) AS dx FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close, close + 1.5 AS high, close - 0.5 AS low FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_efficient_frontier
purpose: Markowitz mean-variance efficient frontier: minimum-variance fully invested portfolios for evenly spaced target returns from the global minimum-variance return to max(mu).
returns: Rows `point_idx`, `expected_return`, `volatility`, `weights` (DOUBLE[]). Long-only by default (interior-point QP polished by an exact KKT solve on the support); `allow_short = true` uses the closed-form unconstrained solution (Merton 1972). `points` (BIGINT, default 25) must be 1 to 100000; points are solved lazily per output chunk. The covariance must be symmetric positive definite; NULL or non-finite inputs raise an error.
example: SELECT * FROM fin_efficient_frontier([0.08, 0.12], [[0.04, 0.006], [0.006, 0.09]], 5, false);

name: fin_ema
purpose: Exponential moving average `ema = k * x + (1 - k) * ema`, `k = 2 / (period + 1)`, seeded with the SMA of the first `period` values (TA-Lib `EMA`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; default period 20. `NULL` for the first `period - 1` rows. 0.3.0 replaced the first-observation seed with the TA-Lib SMA seed. Recursive: depends on every row since the first row (or window frame start). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_ema(close, 10 ORDER BY ts) AS ema FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_ema_halflife
purpose: Time-aware exponential moving average with a half-life.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `sum w_i x_i / sum w_i` with `w_i = 2^(-(t_max - t_i) / halflife)` (pandas `ewm(halflife, times=ts).mean()`, adjust=True), identical to `fin_exp_decay_avg`. `ts` is TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ (DATE casts) with an INTERVAL half-life (months count as 30 days) or numeric with a numeric half-life. Order-independent; runs as a window function. Non-positive half-life raises an error. NULL rows are skipped; a NaN or infinite input makes the group `NULL`. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`.
example: SELECT fin_ema_halflife(x, ts, INTERVAL '1 day') AS ema FROM (VALUES (TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01', 10.0), (TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02', 12.0), (TIMESTAMP '2026-01-03', 11.0)) t(ts, x);

name: fin_entropy
purpose: Shannon entropy of the empirical distribution of `x`.
returns: `DOUBLE` in bits (base-2 plug-in estimator over distinct values, DuckDB `entropy`). NULLs are ignored.
example: SELECT fin_entropy(x) AS entropy_bits FROM (VALUES ('a'), ('a'), ('b'), ('c')) t(x);

name: fin_equal_weights
purpose: Equal portfolio weights: a list of `n` entries of `1 / n`.
returns: `DOUBLE[]`; `n` must be positive, otherwise `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_equal_weights(4) AS weights;

name: fin_ewma_variance
purpose: Annualized RiskMetrics EWMA variance of ordered returns: `s2_t = lambda s2_(t-1) + (1 - lambda) r_t^2`, times `annualization`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; defaults to lambda 0.94 and annualization 252. Seeds with the first non-NULL squared return, then uses `lambda * variance + (1-lambda) * r^2`. Lambda must be in (0,1) and annualization positive and finite, constant within each group. Empty input or an unrepresentable result yields `NULL`. Scaled state avoids intermediate overflow. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Order-dependent native aggregate: pass `ORDER BY` inside the call or use a window `ORDER BY`; rows with equal ordering keys have unspecified relative order, so break ties in the key. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`.
example: SELECT fin_ewma_variance(r, 0.94, 252.0 ORDER BY ts) AS ewma_variance FROM (VALUES (1, 0.01), (2, -0.02), (3, 0.015), (4, -0.005)) t(ts, r);

name: fin_ewma_vol
purpose: Annualized RiskMetrics EWMA volatility of ordered returns: square root of `fin_ewma_variance`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; square root of the EWMA variance model, with the same defaults, seed, and parameter validation as `fin_ewma_variance`. Scaled state can return finite volatility even when variance exceeds DOUBLE range. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Order-dependent native aggregate: pass `ORDER BY` inside the call or use a window `ORDER BY`; rows with equal ordering keys have unspecified relative order, so break ties in the key. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`.
example: SELECT fin_ewma_vol(r, 0.94, 252.0 ORDER BY ts) AS ewma_vol FROM (VALUES (1, 0.01), (2, -0.02), (3, 0.015), (4, -0.005)) t(ts, r);

name: fin_excess_return
purpose: Per-period excess return `r - rf_p`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; scalar SQL macro. `rf_convention` `'annual'` converts geometrically `(1 + rf)^(1/annualization) - 1`; `'periodic'` subtracts `rf` as is; other values raise an error.
example: SELECT fin_excess_return(0.001, 0.05, 252, 'annual') AS excess_return;

name: fin_exp_decay_avg
purpose: Exponentially time-decayed mean.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `sum w_i x_i / sum w_i`, `w_i = 2^(-(t_max - t_i) / halflife)`, `t_max` the latest `ts` in the group or frame. Same argument rules as `fin_ema_halflife`. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`.
example: SELECT fin_exp_decay_avg(x, ts, 2.0) AS decayed_mean FROM (VALUES (1.0, 10.0), (2.0, 12.0), (3.0, 11.0)) t(ts, x);

name: fin_exp_decay_count
purpose: Exponentially time-decayed row count.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `sum 2^(-(t_max - t_i) / halflife)`. `NULL` for an empty group. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`.
example: SELECT fin_exp_decay_count(ts, INTERVAL '1 hour') AS decayed_count FROM (VALUES (TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 09:00:00'), (TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 10:00:00'), (TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 11:00:00')) t(ts);

name: fin_exp_decay_max
purpose: Maximum of exponentially time-decayed values `x_i 2^(-(t_max - t_i) / halflife)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `max_i x_i 2^(-(t_max - t_i) / halflife)`, so older values count less (negative values decay toward zero). Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`.
example: SELECT fin_exp_decay_max(x, ts, 1.0) AS decayed_max FROM (VALUES (1.0, 20.0), (2.0, 12.0), (3.0, 11.0)) t(ts, x);

name: fin_exp_decay_sum
purpose: Exponentially time-decayed sum.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `sum x_i 2^(-(t_max - t_i) / halflife)` in the units of `x`. Same argument rules as `fin_ema_halflife`; runs as a window function. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`.
example: SELECT fin_exp_decay_sum(x, ts, 2.0) AS decayed_sum FROM (VALUES (1.0, 10.0), (2.0, 12.0), (3.0, 11.0)) t(ts, x);

name: fin_expectancy
purpose: Expected return per period `avg(r)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_expectancy(r) AS expectancy FROM (VALUES (0.02), (-0.01), (0.03), (-0.015)) t(r);

name: fin_expected_shortfall
purpose: Positive expected shortfall; alias of `fin_cvar(r, confidence, method, true)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro over the native `fin_cvar`.
example: SELECT fin_expected_shortfall(r, 0.8, 'historical') AS expected_shortfall FROM (VALUES (0.01), (-0.04), (0.02), (-0.01), (0.03), (-0.02), (0.005), (0.015), (-0.03), (0.01)) t(r);

name: fin_factor_alpha
purpose: Annualized single-factor alpha; alias of `fin_alpha`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; see `fin_alpha` (annual decimal risk-free rate).
example: SELECT fin_factor_alpha(r, factor_r, 0.02, 252) AS alpha FROM (VALUES (0.010, 0.008), (-0.020, -0.015), (0.015, 0.010), (0.004, 0.002)) t(r, factor_r);

name: fin_factor_ic
purpose: Information coefficient between factor values and forward returns.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `spearman` (rank IC, default), `pearson` or `kendall` (tau-b). Unknown methods raise an error. Pairs with a NULL are skipped; NaN/inf makes the result `NULL`. Compute per date with `GROUP BY` for a cross-sectional IC series. SQL macro.
example: SELECT fin_factor_ic(factor, forward_return, 'spearman') AS ic FROM (VALUES (1.0, 0.01), (2.0, 0.00), (3.0, 0.02), (4.0, 0.03), (5.0, 0.025)) t(factor, forward_return);

name: fin_factor_report
purpose: Cross-sectional factor diagnostics: per-date Pearson IC, Spearman rank IC, and top-minus-bottom quantile spread, averaged across dates.
returns: One row: `ic` (mean per-date IC), `ic_std`, `ic_ir` (mean/std), `ic_tstat` (mean/(std/sqrt(n_dates))), `rank_ic` (average ranks for ties), `mean_return`, `quantile_spread` (ntile buckets per date ordered by factor then asset), `n_dates` (dates with a defined IC), `n_obs`. Rows with NULL or non-finite factor/return are skipped. `buckets` (BIGINT, default 5) must be 2 to 1000. Every `table_name` argument accepts a table, view, or CTE name, or a parenthesized query such as `'(FROM read_parquet(''t.parquet''))'`.
example: WITH panel AS (SELECT d, asset, (asset * 7 + d * 3) % 10 AS factor, ((asset * 7 + d * 3) % 10) * 0.002 + ((asset + d) % 3) * 0.001 AS fwd FROM range(1, 5) a(asset), range(1, 4) b(d)) SELECT * FROM fin_factor_report('panel', 'd', 'asset', 'factor', 'fwd', 2);

name: fin_factor_turnover
purpose: Factor rank turnover: one minus the mean rank autocorrelation.
returns: `DOUBLE`; ranks `factor` within each `ts` (average ties), correlates each date's ranks with those `period` distinct dates earlier over the assets present on both (alphalens `factor_rank_autocorrelation`), and returns `1 - mean`. Dates with fewer than two common assets are skipped. A duplicate `(ts, asset)` returns `NULL`. 0.3.0 replaced the `stddev_samp(rank)` proxy and its `(factor_rank, period)` signature. SQL macro.
example: SELECT fin_factor_turnover(ts, asset, factor, 1) AS turnover FROM (VALUES (1, 'A', 1.0), (1, 'B', 2.0), (1, 'C', 3.0), (2, 'A', 1.0), (2, 'B', 3.0), (2, 'C', 2.0), (3, 'A', 2.0), (3, 'B', 3.0), (3, 'C', 1.0)) t(ts, asset, factor);

name: fin_fama_macbeth
purpose: Fama-MacBeth (1973) two-pass regression: per-date OLS of y on all `x_cols` with an intercept, then the time-series mean of each coefficient.
returns: One row per coefficient: `term` (`intercept`, then each x column), `estimate`, `stderr`, `tstat` (DOUBLE) and `n_periods` (BIGINT). With `lags` omitted or NULL, `stderr` is the classic `s / sqrt(T)` (sample standard deviation of the per-date estimates); with `lags` given (0 to 100000), it is Newey-West with Bartlett weights `1 - j / (lags + 1)` and no small-sample correction (statsmodels `OLS(b, 1).fit(cov_type='HAC', maxlags=lags, use_correction=False)`). Periods are ordered by the date argument. Rows with a NULL y or x are skipped; dates whose regression is undefined (fewer than k + 1 rows, singular or non-finite) are dropped. 0.3.0 replaced the single-factor per-date output. For the first-pass estimates use `fin_ols(y, [x1, ...])` grouped by date. Every `table_name` argument accepts a table, view, or CTE name, or a parenthesized query such as `'(FROM read_parquet(''t.parquet''))'`.
example: WITH panel AS (SELECT d, asset, (asset * 7 + d * 3) % 10 AS factor, ((asset * 7 + d * 3) % 10) * 0.002 + ((asset + d) % 3) * 0.001 AS fwd FROM range(1, 6) a(asset), range(1, 5) b(d)) SELECT * FROM fin_fama_macbeth('panel', 'd', 'asset', 'fwd', ['factor']);

name: fin_first_non_null
purpose: First non-NULL value when ordered by `ts`.
returns: Type of x; equal `ts` values are ordered by x. Works for any value type; buffers the group's non-NULL values to sort them.
example: SELECT fin_first_non_null(x, ts) AS first_value FROM (VALUES (1, NULL), (2, 12.0), (3, 11.0)) t(ts, x);

name: fin_forward_price
purpose: Cost-of-carry forward price `spot * exp((rate - dividend_yield) * ttm)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; continuous annual rate and dividend yield (default 0), `ttm` in years.
example: SELECT fin_forward_price(100.0, 1.0, 0.05, 0.02) AS forward;

name: fin_forward_rate
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
purpose: Forward rate between `t1` and `t2` implied by discount factors `df1` and `df2`: the rate whose discount factor over `t2 - t1` years is `df2 / df1`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; compounding defaults to `continuous` (`ln(df1 / df2) / (t2 - t1)`); accepts the `fin_parse_compounding` names. `t2 <= t1` or non-positive discount factors return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_forward_rate(0.9608, 0.8869, 1.0, 2.0, 'continuous') AS forward_rate;

name: fin_fra_rate
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
purpose: Forward rate between two zero-rate maturities.
returns: `DOUBLE` = (r2 t2 - r1 t1) / (t2 - t1), the continuously compounded forward implied by continuously compounded zero rates. Requires `t2 > t1`, otherwise `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_fra_rate(0.04, 0.05, 1.0, 2.0) AS forward_rate;

name: fin_from_bps
purpose: Convert basis points to a decimal rate: `bps / 10000`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; inverse of `fin_bps`. `NULL` input gives `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_from_bps(125.0) AS decimal_rate;

name: fin_from_log_return
purpose: Convert a log return to a simple return `expm1(lr)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; uses an `expm1`-accurate form for small values; non-finite input gives `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_from_log_return(0.05) AS simple_return;

name: fin_future_value
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
purpose: Future value `present_value / DF(rate, t)` of an amount after `t` years.
returns: `DOUBLE`; compounding defaults to `continuous` (`pv * exp(rate * t)`); `annual`/`periodic`, `semiannual`, `quarterly`, `monthly` and `simple` are also accepted. Rates at or below -100% for periodic compounding return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_future_value(100.0, 0.05, 2.0, 'annual') AS future_value;

name: fin_gain_to_pain
purpose: Gain-to-pain ratio (Schwager): `sum(r) / abs(sum(r) FILTER (r < 0))`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `NULL` without losses. 0.3.0 fixed it from profit factor to the standard definition. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_gain_to_pain(r) AS gain_to_pain FROM (VALUES (0.02), (-0.01), (0.03), (-0.015)) t(r);

name: fin_garch11_forecast
usage: fin_garch11_forecast(r, omega, alpha, beta ORDER BY ts)
purpose: One-step-ahead GARCH(1,1) variance: filters `sigma2_{t+1} = omega + alpha r_t^2 + beta sigma2_t` through the ordered returns and returns `annualization * sigma2_{n+1}`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `(r, omega, alpha, beta [, initial_var [, annualization]])`. `initial_var` NULL or omitted seeds `sigma2_1` with the sample variance (ddof 1, needs two returns); annualization defaults to 252. omega, alpha, beta must be finite and non-negative and constant within a group. Fit the parameters with `fin_garch_fit`, which uses the same recursion and seed. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Order-dependent native aggregate: pass `ORDER BY` inside the call or use a window `ORDER BY`; rows with equal ordering keys have unspecified relative order, so break ties in the key. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`.
example: SELECT fin_garch11_forecast(r, 0.000002, 0.08, 0.9 ORDER BY ts) AS annualized_variance FROM (VALUES (1, 0.01), (2, -0.02), (3, 0.015), (4, -0.005), (5, 0.007)) t(ts, r);

name: fin_garch_fit
purpose: Maximum-likelihood GARCH(1,1) fit of a zero-mean return series ordered by `order_col`.
returns: One row: `p`, `q`, `nobs` (BIGINT) and `omega`, `alpha`, `beta`, `persistence` (`alpha + beta`), `unconditional_variance` (`omega / (1 - alpha - beta)`), `annualized_vol` (`sqrt(252 * unconditional_variance)`), `loglik` (DOUBLE). Gaussian likelihood with `h_1` the sample variance (ddof 1) and `h_t = omega + alpha r_{t-1}^2 + beta h_{t-1}`, the recursion of `fin_garch11_forecast`; maximized by BFGS over `omega > 0`, `alpha, beta >= 0`, `alpha + beta < 1` from several deterministic starts. Only p = 1, q = 1 and `normal` are accepted. Fewer than 10 rows or any NaN/inf return give NULL parameters. Equal `order_col` values are ordered by return. 0.3.0 added `order_col` and replaced fixed placeholder parameters. Every `table_name` argument accepts a table, view, or CTE name, or a parenthesized query such as `'(FROM read_parquet(''t.parquet''))'`.
example: WITH returns AS (SELECT i AS t, 0.01 * sin(i * 1.7) * (1 + (i % 7) / 3) AS r FROM range(200) t(i)) SELECT * FROM fin_garch_fit('returns', 'r', 't', 1, 1, 'normal');

name: fin_garman_klass_vol
purpose: Garman-Klass (1980) volatility `sqrt(annualization * mean(0.5 ln(H/L)^2 - (2 ln 2 - 1) ln(C/O)^2))`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Bars with non-positive or non-finite prices, high below low, or open/close outside [low, high] make the group `NULL`, as does a negative mean estimator. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_garman_klass_vol(open, high, low, close, 252) AS vol FROM (VALUES (100.0, 102.0, 99.0, 101.0), (101.0, 103.0, 100.5, 102.5), (102.5, 103.0, 100.0, 100.5)) t(open, high, low, close);

name: fin_geometric_return
purpose: Geometric mean per-period return `exp(mean(log1p(r))) - 1`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro, log-space (equals `fin_cagr(r, 1)`).
example: SELECT fin_geometric_return(r) AS geometric_mean FROM (VALUES (0.10), (-0.05), (0.08)) t(r);

name: fin_gross_return
purpose: Gross return `1 + r` of a decimal simple return.
returns: `DOUBLE`; scalar SQL macro; `NULL` input gives `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_gross_return(r) AS gross_return FROM (VALUES (0.10), (-0.05), (0.08)) t(r);

name: fin_half_life_mean_reversion
purpose: Half-life of mean reversion from an AR(1) fit.
returns: `DOUBLE` in rows of `ts`; regresses `x_t - x_{t-1}` on a constant and `x_{t-1}`, `phi = 1 + slope`, half-life `ln(0.5) / ln(phi)` (the continuous approximation `-ln 2 / slope` differs for fast reversion). `NULL` unless `0 < phi < 1` or with fewer than three rows. Rows are ordered by `ts` (integer, DOUBLE, DATE, TIMESTAMP or TIMESTAMPTZ); ties on `ts` are ordered by value, so results never depend on row order or threads. Rows with a NULL argument are skipped; a NaN or infinite input makes the group `NULL`. 0.3.0 added `ts`. SQL macro.
example: SELECT fin_half_life_mean_reversion(x, ts) AS half_life FROM (VALUES (1, 1.0), (2, 0.6), (3, 0.5), (4, 0.2), (5, 0.25), (6, 0.05), (7, 0.1), (8, -0.05)) t(ts, x);

name: fin_hit_ratio
purpose: Fraction of observations above the per-period threshold.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. `threshold` is annual; Rates are annual decimals converted geometrically to per-period rates, `(1 + rate)^(1/annualization) - 1`. 0.3.0 changed it from per-period to annual and added `annualization`. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_hit_ratio(r, 0.0, 252) AS hit_ratio FROM (VALUES (0.02), (-0.01), (0.03), (-0.015)) t(r);

name: fin_hma
purpose: Hull moving average `WMA(2 * WMA(x, floor(period / 2)) - WMA(x, period), floor(sqrt(period)))` (Alan Hull; not part of TA-Lib).
returns: `DOUBLE`; default period 20 (minimum 2). First value at row `period + floor(sqrt(period)) - 2`. Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_hma(close, 16 ORDER BY ts) AS hma FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_hrp_weights
purpose: Hierarchical risk parity weights (Lopez de Prado 2016) from a covariance matrix.
returns: Rows `asset_idx`, `asset` (label or NULL), `weight` summing to 1. Follows PyPortfolioOpt HRPOpt: correlation distance sqrt((1 - rho) / 2), scipy-style agglomerative linkage (`single` default, `complete`, `average`, `ward`), dendrogram leaf order, recursive bisection with inverse-variance cluster variance. Exact distance ties may order leaves differently from scipy. The matrix must be square, symmetric, finite, with a positive diagonal; labels must match its size.

name: fin_hurst
purpose: Hurst exponent by rescaled-range (R/S) analysis.
returns: `DOUBLE`; for window sizes 8, 16, 32, ... (at least two windows each) averages R/S over non-overlapping windows (population standard deviation, no Anis-Lloyd correction) and returns the slope of `log(R/S)` on `log(size)`. Pass increments (returns), not prices. Needs at least 32 rows. Rows are ordered by `ts` (integer, DOUBLE, DATE, TIMESTAMP or TIMESTAMPTZ); ties on `ts` are ordered by value, so results never depend on row order or threads. Rows with a NULL argument are skipped; a NaN or infinite input makes the group `NULL`. 0.3.0 replaced the fixed 0.5 placeholder and added `ts`. SQL macro.
example: SELECT fin_hurst(x, ts) AS hurst FROM (SELECT i AS ts, sin(i * 1.3) + 0.5 * sin(i * 0.37) AS x FROM range(64) t(i));

name: fin_imbalance_bars
purpose: Fixed-threshold volume imbalance bars (AFML ch. 2.3.2): the bar closes once abs(sum of signed volume) reaches the threshold.
returns: Rows are ordered by (`asset_col`, ts, `seq_col`, price, volume), so ties are deterministic; rows with NULL ts or price (or NULL volume for volume-based bars) are skipped. AFML reset-accumulator convention (Lopez de Prado 2018, ch. 2.3): the bar closes on the first row whose running total reaches the threshold (relative tolerance 1e-12) and the next bar restarts at zero, so overshoot does not carry over. Returns [asset_col,] `bar_id` (0-based per asset), `start_ts`, `end_ts`, `open`, `high`, `low`, `close`, `volume`, `vwap`, `ticks`; the last bar of each asset may be incomplete. Method `signed` (default) reads the volume column as signed (buy positive, sell negative); `tick_rule` signs non-negative volume by the tick rule (sign of the last non-zero price change, 0 before the first change). Extra `imbalance` column is the signed total at close; `volume` is traded (absolute) volume. The AFML expected-imbalance (EWMA) threshold is not implemented; pass a fixed threshold. Named `asset_col`, `seq_col`. Every `table_name` argument accepts a table, view, or CTE name, or a parenthesized query such as `'(FROM read_parquet(''t.parquet''))'`.
