purpose: Extended parabolic SAR (TA-Lib `SAREXT`) with positional `start_value` (0 = automatic direction, > 0 start long at that SAR, < 0 start short at its absolute value), `offset_on_reverse`, `af_init_long`, `af_long`, `af_max_long`, `af_init_short`, `af_short`, `af_max_short`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; short positions are returned as negative values, as in TA-Lib. All parameters are optional with the defaults shown. First value at row 1. 0.3.0 replaced the unused `options` argument with the TA-Lib parameters. Recursive: depends on every row since the first row (or window frame start). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_sarext(high, low, 0, 0, 0.02, 0.02, 0.2, 0.02, 0.02, 0.2 ORDER BY ts) AS sar FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 101 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS high, 99 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS low FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_schema_template
purpose: Return the expected columns for a named finance schema template (`ohlcv`, `returns`, `option_chain`, `rates_curve`, `portfolio`).
returns: Table with `schema_kind`, `column_name`, `logical_type`, `required`, `description`. Unknown or NULL kinds raise an error.
example: SELECT * FROM fin_schema_template('ohlcv');

name: fin_semivariance
purpose: Per-period downside semivariance `mean(min(r - T_p, 0)^2)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro, not annualized. `threshold` is annual; Rates are annual decimals converted geometrically to per-period rates, `(1 + rate)^(1/annualization) - 1`. 0.3.0 changed it from per-period to annual. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_semivariance(r, 0.0, 252) AS semivariance FROM (VALUES (0.01), (-0.02), (0.015), (-0.005)) t(r);

name: fin_session_date
purpose: Return the exchange-local calendar date of a timestamp.
returns: `DATE`; `TIMESTAMPTZ` values are converted from UTC to the calendar's exchange zone, `TIMESTAMP` values are read in the optional zone argument (default: exchange zone). Infinite timestamps and timezone shifts outside the finite TIMESTAMP range return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_session_date(TIMESTAMP '2026-05-06 23:30:00', 'NYSE', 'UTC') AS session_date;

name: fin_sharpe
purpose: Annualized Sharpe ratio `mean(e) / stddev_samp(e) * sqrt(annualization)` with `e = r - rf_p`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `(r [, risk_free [, annualization]])`. `risk_free` is annual (constant or per-row); Rates are annual decimals converted geometrically to per-period rates, `(1 + rate)^(1/annualization) - 1`. `NULL` for fewer than two observations or zero dispersion. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.

name: fin_simple_return
purpose: Simple return `price / prev_price - 1` between two prices.
returns: `DOUBLE`; scalar SQL macro. `NULL` prices or a zero `prev_price` give `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_simple_return(105.0, 100.0) AS simple_return;

name: fin_sma
purpose: Simple moving average: mean of the last `period` values (TA-Lib `SMA`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `period` (default 20). `NULL` for the first `period - 1` rows. 0.3.0 made `period` effective (it was ignored). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_sma(close, 20 ORDER BY ts) AS sma FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_sortino
purpose: Annualized Sortino ratio: mean excess return over the per-period MAR divided by downside deviation, times `sqrt(annualization)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; defaults to MAR 0 and 252 observations per year. Excess return `r - mar_p`; MAR is annual; Rates are annual decimals converted geometrically to per-period rates, `(1 + rate)^(1/annualization) - 1`. 0.3.0 changed the conversion from `mar / annualization`. Downside deviation uses all observations in its denominator. Annualization must be positive, finite, and constant within each group. Empty input or no downside yields `NULL`. Scaled, compensated state supports very large and tiny returns. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`.
example: SELECT fin_sortino(r, 0.0, 252) AS sortino FROM (VALUES (0.010), (-0.004), (0.006), (-0.002), (0.008)) t(r);

name: fin_spread
purpose: Quoted spread `ask - bid`.
returns: `DOUBLE` scalar. Crossed quotes give `NULL` (0.3.0; previously a negative spread).
example: SELECT fin_spread(99.98, 100.02) AS spread;

name: fin_spread_bps
purpose: Quoted spread in basis points of the midpoint `(ask - bid) / ((bid + ask) / 2) * 10000`.
returns: `DOUBLE` scalar. Crossed quotes or a non-positive midpoint give `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_spread_bps(99.98, 100.02) AS spread_bps;

name: fin_stability
purpose: Stability of returns (empyrical `stability_of_timeseries`): R^2 of an OLS fit of cumulative log returns on the observation index.
returns: `DOUBLE` in [0, 1]; `NULL` for fewer than two returns or constant cumulative returns. Returns at or below -1 make the group `NULL`. 0.3.0 replaced the constant placeholder. Order-dependent native aggregate: pass `ORDER BY` inside the call or use a window `ORDER BY`; rows with equal ordering keys have unspecified relative order, so break ties in the key. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`.
example: SELECT fin_stability(r ORDER BY ts) AS stability FROM (VALUES (1, 0.010), (2, 0.004), (3, 0.006), (4, -0.002), (5, 0.008)) t(ts, r);

name: fin_stable_corr
purpose: Sample correlation via DuckDB `corr`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Non-finite input or a constant series makes the group `NULL`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_stable_corr(y, x) AS corr FROM (VALUES (1.0, 1.0), (2.1, 2.0), (2.9, 3.0), (4.2, 4.0)) t(y, x);

name: fin_stable_cov
purpose: Sample covariance via DuckDB `covar_samp`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_stable_cov(y, x) AS cov FROM (VALUES (1.0, 1.0), (2.1, 2.0), (2.9, 3.0), (4.2, 4.0)) t(y, x);

name: fin_stable_mean
purpose: Mean with a compensated (`fsum`) numerator.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_stable_mean(x) AS mean FROM (VALUES (1e9 + 1.0), (1e9 + 2.0), (1e9 + 3.0)) t(x);

name: fin_stable_stddev
purpose: Square root of `fin_stable_var`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_stable_stddev(x, 1) AS stddev FROM (VALUES (1.0), (2.0), (4.0)) t(x);

name: fin_stable_var
purpose: Variance with denominator `count(x) - ddof`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Any finite non-negative `ddof`; an exhausted denominator returns `NULL`. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_stable_var(x, 0) AS population_variance FROM (VALUES (1.0), (2.0), (4.0)) t(x);

name: fin_stddev
purpose: Rolling standard deviation of the last `period` values, population by default (TA-Lib `STDDEV` with nbdev 1).
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `period` (20) and `ddof` (0 = population, 1 = sample; must be smaller than `period`). `NULL` for the first `period - 1` rows. 0.3.0 changed the default `ddof` from 1 to 0 and made `period` effective. Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_stddev(close, 20, 0 ORDER BY ts) AS stddev FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_stoch
usage: fin_stoch(high, low, close, 14, 3, 3 ORDER BY ts)
purpose: Slow stochastic oscillator: `fastK = 100 * (close - LL) / (HH - LL)` over the last `k` rows, `k = SMA(fastK, smooth)` and `d = SMA(k, d)` (TA-Lib `STOCH` with SMA smoothing; fastk_period = `k`, slowk_period = `smooth`, slowd_period = `d`).
returns: `STRUCT(k DOUBLE, d DOUBLE)`; positional `k` (14), `d` (3), `smooth` (3); `smooth = 1` gives the fast stochastic. `NULL` for the first `k + smooth + d - 3` rows. A flat high-low range gives fastK 0 (TA-Lib). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_stoch(high, low, close, 14, 3, 3 ORDER BY ts) AS stoch FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close, close + 1.5 AS high, close - 0.5 AS low FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_stochrsi
purpose: Stochastic RSI: `k = 100 * (RSI - min RSI) / (max RSI - min RSI)` over the last `k` RSI(`period`) values and `d = SMA(k, d)` (TA-Lib `STOCHRSI` with fastk_period = `k`, fastd_period = `d`).
returns: `STRUCT(k DOUBLE, d DOUBLE)`; positional `period` (14), `k` (3), `d` (3). `NULL` for the first `period + k + d - 2` rows. A flat RSI range gives 0. Recursive: depends on every row since the first row (or window frame start). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_stochrsi(close, 14, 3, 3 ORDER BY ts) AS stochrsi FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_student_t_cdf
purpose: Evaluate the Student-t CDF.
returns: `DOUBLE` in [0, 1]; regularized incomplete beta evaluated in log space, accurate in deep tails and for very large `df` (infinite `df` is the normal CDF). Non-positive `df` returns `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_student_t_cdf(2.228139, 10.0) AS p;

name: fin_student_t_inv
purpose: Invert the Student-t CDF.
returns: `DOUBLE`; closed forms for `df` 1 and 2, otherwise safeguarded Newton on the log tail. `p` must be in (0, 1); deep tails such as `p = 1e-100` stay finite. Invalid inputs return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_student_t_inv(0.975, 10.0) AS t;

name: fin_svi_total_variance
purpose: Raw SVI total implied variance `w(k) = a + b (rho (k - m) + sqrt((k - m)^2 + sigma^2))` at log-moneyness `k` (Gatheral 2004).
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `(k, a, b, rho, m, sigma)`. `w` is variance times time to expiry.
example: SELECT fin_svi_total_variance(0.1, 0.02, 0.1, -0.3, 0.0, 0.2) AS total_variance;

name: fin_svi_vol
purpose: Implied volatility `sqrt(w(k) / ttm)` from the raw SVI total-variance slice.
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `(k, ttm, a, b, rho, m, sigma)`. `ttm <= 0` or negative total variance returns `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_svi_vol(0.1, 0.5, 0.02, 0.1, -0.3, 0.0, 0.2) AS implied_vol;

name: fin_swap_rate
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
purpose: Par swap rate from annual payment times and discount factors.
returns: `DOUBLE` = (1 - last DF) / sum(accrual x DF). Maturities must be positive and strictly increasing and discount factors positive and finite, otherwise `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_swap_rate([1.0, 2.0, 3.0], [0.96, 0.92, 0.88]) AS par_rate;

name: fin_t3
purpose: Tillson T3: six chained SMA-seeded EMAs combined as `c1 e6 + c2 e5 + c3 e4 + c4 e3` with volume-factor coefficients (TA-Lib `T3`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `period` (default 20) and `vfactor` in [0, 1] (default 0.7). First value at row `6 * (period - 1)`. Recursive: depends on every row since the first row (or window frame start). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_t3(close, 5, 0.7 ORDER BY ts) AS t3 FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_tail_ratio
purpose: Tail ratio `quantile(r, upper_q) / abs(quantile(r, lower_q))` (linear interpolation).
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro computing both quantiles in one sort. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`.

name: fin_tema
purpose: Triple exponential moving average `3 * EMA1 - 3 * EMA2 + EMA3` of chained, SMA-seeded EMA stages (TA-Lib `TEMA`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; default period 20. First value at row `3 * (period - 1)`. Recursive: depends on every row since the first row (or window frame start). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_tema(close, 10 ORDER BY ts) AS tema FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_theils_u
purpose: Theil's uncertainty coefficient U(x given y).
returns: `DOUBLE` in [0, 1]: `(H(x) - H(x given y)) / H(x)` with natural logs; asymmetric. Categories of any type are hashed; NULL rows are skipped. Constant `x` (zero entropy) returns `NULL`. SQL macro.
example: SELECT fin_theils_u(x, y) AS theils_u FROM (VALUES ('a', 'u'), ('a', 'u'), ('b', 'v'), ('b', 'v'), ('a', 'v'), ('b', 'u')) t(x, y);

name: fin_tick_bars
purpose: Aggregate trades into tick bars of `ceil(threshold)` rows (default threshold 100).
returns: Rows are ordered by (`asset_col`, ts, `seq_col`, price, volume), so ties are deterministic; rows with NULL ts or price (or NULL volume for volume-based bars) are skipped. AFML reset-accumulator convention (Lopez de Prado 2018, ch. 2.3): the bar closes on the first row whose running total reaches the threshold (relative tolerance 1e-12) and the next bar restarts at zero, so overshoot does not carry over. Returns [asset_col,] `bar_id` (0-based per asset), `start_ts`, `end_ts`, `open`, `high`, `low`, `close`, `volume`, `vwap`, `ticks`; the last bar of each asset may be incomplete. `volume` and `vwap` are NULL unless named `volume_col := 'col'` is given. Named `asset_col`, `seq_col`, `volume_col`. Every `table_name` argument accepts a table, view, or CTE name, or a parenthesized query such as `'(FROM read_parquet(''t.parquet''))'`.
example: WITH ticks AS (SELECT TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 09:30:00' + i * INTERVAL '20 seconds' AS ts, 100 + (i % 5) * 0.1 AS price, 100.0 + 50 * (i % 3) AS volume FROM range(12) t(i)) SELECT * FROM fin_tick_bars('ticks', 'ts', 'price', 4, volume_col := 'volume');

name: fin_to_log_return
purpose: Convert a simple return to a log return `log1p(r)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; uses a `log1p`-accurate form for small values; returns at or below -1 and non-finite input give `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_to_log_return(0.05) AS log_return;

name: fin_total_return
purpose: Compound decimal simple or log returns in log space: `expm1(sum(log1p(r)))` or `expm1(sum(r))`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; optional method `'simple'` or `'log'` (other values raise an error, even on empty input). Skips NULL observations. A simple return of -1 produces total loss; returns below -1, non-finite observations, overflow and empty groups return `NULL`. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_total_return(r, 'simple') AS total_return FROM (VALUES (0.01), (0.02), (-0.01)) t(r);

name: fin_tracking_error
purpose: Annualized tracking error `stddev_samp(r - b) * sqrt(annualization)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_tracking_error(r, benchmark_r, 252) AS tracking_error FROM (VALUES (0.010, 0.008), (-0.020, -0.015), (0.015, 0.010), (0.004, 0.002)) t(r, benchmark_r);

name: fin_trade_sign
purpose: Trade initiator sign: +1 buyer-initiated, -1 seller-initiated, 0 unclassified. Method `'lee_ready'` (default, Lee and Ready 1991): above the quote midpoint +1, below -1, at the midpoint the tick test against `prev_price`. Method `'emo'` (Ellis, Michaely and O'Hara 2000): at or above the ask +1, at or below the bid -1, otherwise the tick test.
returns: `DOUBLE` scalar. A `NULL` `prev_price` leaves the tick test unclassified (0) but quote-based classifications still apply; pass the last different trade price for Lee-Ready's zero-tick rule. Crossed quotes or non-finite inputs give `NULL`. `method` must be a constant; unknown methods raise an error. 0.3.0 BREAKING: the default rule is Lee-Ready (0.2 used the EMO touch rule, now `'emo'`), a `NULL` previous price no longer nulls the result, and NaN prices give `NULL` instead of 0.
example: SELECT fin_trade_sign(100.03, 99.98, 100.02, 100.01, 'lee_ready') AS sign;

name: fin_treynor_ratio
purpose: Treynor ratio `avg(r - rf_p) * annualization / beta` over complete pairs.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. `risk_free` is annual; Rates are annual decimals converted geometrically to per-period rates, `(1 + rate)^(1/annualization) - 1`. 0.3.0 uses the same complete pairs as beta and subtracts the per-period rate before annualizing. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_treynor_ratio(r, benchmark_r, 0.02, 252) AS treynor FROM (VALUES (0.010, 0.008), (-0.020, -0.015), (0.015, 0.010), (0.004, 0.002)) t(r, benchmark_r);

name: fin_trima
purpose: Triangular moving average: triangular weights `1, 2, ..., 2, 1` over the last `period` values, computed as an SMA of an SMA (TA-Lib `TRIMA`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; default period 20. `NULL` for the first `period - 1` rows. Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_trima(close, 20 ORDER BY ts) AS trima FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_trimmed_mean
purpose: Average observations between the inclusive lower and upper continuous quantiles.
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `(x [, lower_q, upper_q])`, defaults 0.05 and 0.95; bounds must satisfy `0 <= lower_q <= upper_q <= 1`. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_trimmed_mean(x, 0.1, 0.9) AS trimmed_mean FROM (VALUES (1.0), (2.0), (3.0), (4.0), (100.0)) t(x);

name: fin_trix
purpose: 1-row rate of change in percent of a triple-smoothed, SMA-seeded EMA (TA-Lib `TRIX`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; default period 30. First value at row `3 * (period - 1) + 1`; `NULL` when the previous triple EMA is 0. Recursive: depends on every row since the first row (or window frame start). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_trix(close, 10 ORDER BY ts) AS trix FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_true_range
usage: fin_true_range(high, low, close ORDER BY ts)
purpose: True range of the last row, `max(high - low, abs(high - previous close), abs(low - previous close))` (TA-Lib `TRANGE`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; no parameters. `NULL` for the first row (no previous close). 0.3.0 replaced the group range `max(high) - min(low)`. Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_true_range(high, low, close ORDER BY ts) AS true_range FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close, close + 1.5 AS high, close - 0.5 AS low FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_ts_grid_spec
usage: fin_ts_grid_spec(start_ts, end_ts, step, staleness := NULL, method := 'last')
purpose: Pack a time-grid start, end, positive step, staleness and sampling method into a validated spec struct.
returns: `STRUCT(start_ts TIMESTAMP, end_ts TIMESTAMP, step INTERVAL, staleness INTERVAL, method VARCHAR)`. Errors for a non-positive step, `end_ts < start_ts`, negative staleness or a method other than `last`.
example: SELECT fin_ts_grid_spec(TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 09:30:00', TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 16:00:00', INTERVAL '5 minutes') AS spec;

name: fin_tsf
purpose: Time series forecast: the least-squares line over the last `period` values extrapolated one row ahead, `intercept + slope * period` (TA-Lib `TSF`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; default period 14 (minimum 2). `NULL` for the first `period - 1` rows. Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_tsf(close, 14 ORDER BY ts) AS forecast FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_ttest_1samp
purpose: One-sample Student t test of the mean against `mu`.
returns: `STRUCT(stat, pvalue, df)` of DOUBLE; `t = (mean - mu) / (s / sqrt(n))`, `df = n - 1`, two-sided p-value from the Student t distribution (scipy `ttest_1samp`). Fewer than two rows, zero variance or NaN/inf input return `NULL`. SQL macro.
example: SELECT fin_ttest_1samp(x, 0.0) AS ttest FROM (VALUES (0.5), (1.2), (0.8), (1.5), (0.9)) t(x);

name: fin_ttest_2samp
purpose: Two-sample t test of equal means.
returns: `STRUCT(stat, pvalue, df)` of DOUBLE. `equal_var := true` uses the pooled variance and `df = n_x + n_y - 2`; `false` is Welch's test with Welch-Satterthwaite `df`. Two-sided p-value (scipy `ttest_ind`). `x` and `y` are separate columns with independent NULLs; each needs two rows. NaN/inf input returns `NULL`. SQL macro.
example: SELECT fin_ttest_2samp(x, y, true) AS ttest FROM (VALUES (1.0, 2.0), (2.0, 3.0), (3.0, 4.5), (2.5, 3.5)) t(x, y);

name: fin_turnover
purpose: One-way portfolio turnover `sum(abs(new_i - old_i)) / 2` between two weight vectors.
returns: `DOUBLE`; native scalar. Lists of different lengths return `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_turnover([0.5, 0.3, 0.2], [0.4, 0.4, 0.2]) AS turnover;

name: fin_twap
purpose: Time-weighted average price: each price holds from its timestamp until the next distinct timestamp, `sum(price_k * (t_{k+1} - t_k)) / (t_last - t_first)`; the last timestamp carries no weight.
returns: `DOUBLE`; `ts` is `TIMESTAMP`, `TIMESTAMPTZ`, `DATE` or numeric. Prices sharing a timestamp are averaged, so ties do not depend on row order; a single timestamp returns its mean price. Rows must reach the aggregate in time order: use `ORDER BY ts` inside the call or a window ordered by `ts`; out-of-order input raises `fin_twap: rows reached the aggregate out of time order`. Non-finite prices or timestamps make the result `NULL`. 0.3.0 replaced `avg(price)`, which ignored `ts`.
example: SELECT fin_twap(price, ts ORDER BY ts) AS twap FROM (VALUES (TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 09:30:00', 100.0), (TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 09:30:40', 101.0), (TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 09:31:00', 100.5)) t(ts, price);

name: fin_typ_price
purpose: Typical price `(high + low + close) / 3` (TA-Lib `TYPPRICE`).
returns: `DOUBLE` scalar; `NULL` input or non-finite result gives `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_typ_price(102.0, 99.0, 101.0) AS typical_price;

name: fin_typeof
purpose: Return the DuckDB logical type name of the argument (DuckDB `typeof`).
returns: `VARCHAR`, for example `DECIMAL(2,1)` for the literal `1.5`; scalar SQL macro.
example: SELECT fin_typeof(1.5) AS type_name;

name: fin_ulcer_index
purpose: Ulcer index `sqrt(mean(D_t^2))` of the fractional drawdown series.
returns: `DOUBLE` >= 0 (fractions, not percent). Order-dependent native aggregate: pass `ORDER BY` inside the call or use a window `ORDER BY`; rows with equal ordering keys have unspecified relative order, so break ties in the key. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_ulcer_index(r ORDER BY ts) AS ulcer_index FROM (VALUES (1, 0.05), (2, -0.10), (3, 0.02), (4, -0.03), (5, 0.08)) t(ts, r);

name: fin_ultosc
usage: fin_ultosc(high, low, close, 7, 14, 28 ORDER BY ts)
purpose: Ultimate oscillator `100 * (4 A1 + 2 A2 + A3) / 7` with `Ak = sum(BP) / sum(TR)` over the three periods sorted ascending, buying pressure `BP = close - min(low, previous close)` (TA-Lib `ULTOSC`).
returns: `DOUBLE` in [0, 100]; positional `short`, `medium`, `long` (7, 14, 28). First value at row `max(periods)`; a zero true-range sum drops its term (TA-Lib). Bounded: depends on the last `max(periods) + 1` rows. 0.3.0 replaced `100 * avg((C - L) / (H - L))` and honors the periods. Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_ultosc(high, low, close, 7, 14, 28 ORDER BY ts) AS ultosc FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close, close + 1.5 AS high, close - 0.5 AS low FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_up_capture
purpose: Up-market capture `avg(r) FILTER (b > 0) / avg(b) FILTER (b > 0)` over complete pairs.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_up_capture(r, benchmark_r) AS up_capture FROM (VALUES (0.010, 0.008), (-0.020, -0.015), (0.015, 0.010), (0.004, 0.002)) t(r, benchmark_r);

name: fin_upside_deviation
purpose: Annualized upside deviation `sqrt(mean(max(r - T_p, 0)^2)) * sqrt(annualization)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. `threshold` is annual; Rates are annual decimals converted geometrically to per-period rates, `(1 + rate)^(1/annualization) - 1`. 0.3.0 changed it from per-period to annual. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_upside_deviation(r, 0.0, 252) AS upside_deviation FROM (VALUES (0.01), (-0.02), (0.015), (-0.005)) t(r);

name: fin_validate_curve_spec
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
purpose: Validate the numerical inputs used by curve interpolation.
returns: `STRUCT(ok, reason)`; requires non-empty, equal-length lists, finite non-null values, and strictly increasing finite maturities. Reports the failed constraint. It does not validate pricing-model metadata.
example: SELECT fin_validate_curve_spec(fin_curve_spec([1.0, 0.5], [0.04, 0.05])) AS check;

name: fin_validate_ohlc
purpose: Validate an OHLC bar.
returns: STRUCT(`ok`, `reason`); rejects NULL or non-finite inputs, non-positive prices, high below open/close/low, and low above open/close.
example: SELECT fin_validate_ohlc(100.0, 101.0, 99.0, 100.5) AS valid_bar, fin_validate_ohlc(100.0, 99.0, 101.0, 100.5) AS invalid_bar;

name: fin_validate_option_spec
purpose: Validate an option spec before pricing.
returns: STRUCT(`ok` BOOLEAN, `reason` VARCHAR). `ok` is false (never `NULL`) for a `NULL` spec, kind other than call/put, non-positive or non-finite spot or strike, negative or non-finite ttm or vol, or non-finite rate or dividend yield; `reason` names the first failing field.
example: SELECT fin_validate_option_spec(fin_option_spec('call', 100.0, 100.0, 0.0, 0.05, 0.2)) AS check;

name: fin_validate_rate_spec
purpose: Validate a rate spec and report the first failed rule.
returns: `STRUCT(ok BOOLEAN, reason VARCHAR)`. Checks, in order: rate finite, rate > -1, rate <= 1 (larger values look like percentages), canonical compounding (`continuous`, `simple`, `periodic`, `semiannual`, `quarterly`, `monthly`, `daily`), canonical day count (`ACT/365F`, `ACT/360`, `ACT/ACT`, `ACT/ACT ICMA`, `30/360`, `30U/360`, `30E/360`), and integer frequency >= 1. `reason` is `ok` when valid.
example: SELECT fin_validate_rate_spec(fin_rate_spec(0.05)) AS check;

name: fin_validate_return
purpose: Check that a decimal return is plausible.
returns: `BOOLEAN`; true for finite returns with r >= -1 (a total loss of -1 is valid) and abs(r) <= `max_abs`, an optional second argument that defaults to 1.0.
example: SELECT fin_validate_return(0.05) AS ok, fin_validate_return(-1.5) AS below_total_loss;

name: fin_validate_schema
purpose: Validate a table's columns against a schema template.
returns: One row per template column: `expected_type`, `required`, `present`, `actual_type`, `compatible` (any numeric for DOUBLE, DATE or TIMESTAMP variants for temporal columns), `status` (`ok`, `missing`, `missing_optional`, `type_mismatch`), and `valid`. Names match case-insensitively. Unknown kinds or missing tables raise an error. Every `table_name` argument accepts a table, view, or CTE name, or a parenthesized query such as `'(FROM read_parquet(''t.parquet''))'`.
example: WITH returns AS (SELECT DATE '2026-01-02' AS date, 'AAA' AS asset_id, 0.01 AS return_decimal) SELECT * FROM fin_validate_schema('returns', 'returns');

name: fin_var
purpose: Value at risk at the given confidence.
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `(r [, confidence [, method [, loss_positive]]])` with defaults 0.95, `'historical'`, `true`. `historical`: linear-interpolation `1 - confidence` quantile (positions within 1e-9 of an order statistic snap to it). `parametric`: `mean + sd * z` (sample sd, normal quantile). `cornish_fisher`: modified VaR with population skewness and excess kurtosis (Zangari 1996). Unknown methods and confidence outside (0, 1) raise an error. Positive loss by default. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.

name: fin_var_indicator
purpose: Rolling variance of the last `period` values, population by default (TA-Lib `VAR`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `period` (20) and `ddof` (default 0; must be smaller than `period`). `NULL` for the first `period - 1` rows. 0.3.0 changed the default `ddof` from 1 to 0 and made `period` effective. Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_var_indicator(close, 20, 0 ORDER BY ts) AS variance FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_var_spec
purpose: Pack a VaR confidence in (0, 1), method (`historical`, `parametric`, `cornish_fisher`) and tail convention into a spec struct.
returns: `STRUCT(confidence DOUBLE, method VARCHAR, tail VARCHAR, loss_positive BOOLEAN)`. `method` is `historical`, `parametric` or `cornish_fisher` (as in `fin_var`); errors for unknown methods or tails and confidence outside (0, 1).
example: SELECT fin_var_spec(0.99, 'parametric') AS spec;

name: fin_vector_add
purpose: Element-wise sum of two equal-length lists.
returns: `DOUBLE[]`; a length mismatch returns `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_vector_add([1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]) AS total;

name: fin_vector_mean
purpose: Arithmetic mean of a list's elements.
returns: `DOUBLE`; an empty list returns `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_vector_mean([1.0, 2.0, 6.0]) AS mean;

name: fin_vector_normalize_sum
purpose: Scale a list so that its elements sum to one: `x_i / sum(x)`.
returns: `DOUBLE[]`; a zero or non-finite sum returns `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_vector_normalize_sum([2.0, 1.0, 1.0]) AS weights;

name: fin_vector_scale
purpose: Multiply every element of a list by a scalar.
returns: `DOUBLE[]`.
example: SELECT fin_vector_scale([1.0, 2.0], 0.5) AS scaled;

name: fin_vector_sub
purpose: Element-wise difference `a - b` of two equal-length lists.
returns: `DOUBLE[]`; a length mismatch returns `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_vector_sub([3.0, 4.0], [1.0, 2.0]) AS difference;

name: fin_vector_sum
purpose: Sum of a list's elements.
returns: `DOUBLE`; an empty list returns `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_vector_sum([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]) AS total;

name: fin_version
purpose: Return the loaded finance extension version string.
returns: VARCHAR in `finance <version>` form for releases.
example: SELECT fin_version() AS version;

name: fin_vol_of_vol
purpose: Annualized dispersion of a volatility series `stddev_samp(vol) * sqrt(annualization)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_vol_of_vol(vol, 252) AS vol_of_vol FROM (VALUES (0.20), (0.22), (0.19), (0.25)) t(vol);

name: fin_volatility
purpose: Annualized volatility `sqrt(sum((r - mean)^2) / (n - ddof)) * sqrt(annualization)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `(r [, annualization [, ddof]])`, defaults 252 and 1. `NULL` when `n <= ddof`. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_volatility(r, 252, 1) AS volatility FROM (VALUES (0.010), (-0.004), (0.006), (0.002), (0.008)) t(r);

name: fin_volume_bars
purpose: Aggregate trades into volume bars that close once accumulated volume reaches the threshold.
returns: Rows are ordered by (`asset_col`, ts, `seq_col`, price, volume), so ties are deterministic; rows with NULL ts or price (or NULL volume for volume-based bars) are skipped. AFML reset-accumulator convention (Lopez de Prado 2018, ch. 2.3): the bar closes on the first row whose running total reaches the threshold (relative tolerance 1e-12) and the next bar restarts at zero, so overshoot does not carry over. Returns [asset_col,] `bar_id` (0-based per asset), `start_ts`, `end_ts`, `open`, `high`, `low`, `close`, `volume`, `vwap`, `ticks`; the last bar of each asset may be incomplete. Volume must be finite and non-negative and the threshold positive, else an error. Named `asset_col`, `seq_col`. Every `table_name` argument accepts a table, view, or CTE name, or a parenthesized query such as `'(FROM read_parquet(''t.parquet''))'`.
example: WITH ticks AS (SELECT TIMESTAMP '2026-01-02 09:30:00' + i * INTERVAL '20 seconds' AS ts, 100 + (i % 5) * 0.1 AS price, 100.0 + 50 * (i % 3) AS volume FROM range(12) t(i)) SELECT * FROM fin_volume_bars('ticks', 'ts', 'price', 'volume', 500.0);

name: fin_volume_profile
purpose: Volume per equal-width price bin over `[min(price), max(price)]`; bin `i` covers `[min + i w, min + (i + 1) w)` with `w = (max - min) / bins`, the last bin closed.
returns: `LIST(STRUCT(price_low DOUBLE, price_high DOUBLE, volume DOUBLE))` with `bins` entries (one entry when all prices are equal); positional constant `bins` (10, 1..100000). Exact per distinct price up to 4096 distinct prices; beyond that prices are pre-aggregated on at most 4096 power-of-two-width cells spanning the range and each cell goes to the bin holding its midpoint, so volume near a bin edge can move to the adjacent bin by at most one cell width (`< (max - min) / 2048`). Memory is bounded and results do not depend on row order. Rows with a `NULL` price or volume are skipped; non-finite input or negative volume makes the group `NULL`. Order-independent native aggregate. 0.3.0 replaced `histogram(price)`, which ignored volume and bins.
example: SELECT fin_volume_profile(price, volume, 3) AS profile FROM (VALUES (100.0, 200.0), (100.5, 100.0), (101.0, 300.0), (101.5, 50.0), (102.0, 150.0)) t(price, volume);

name: fin_vpin
usage: fin_vpin(signed_volume, volume, 50, bucket_volume ORDER BY ts)
purpose: Volume-synchronized probability of informed trading (Easley, Lopez de Prado and O'Hara 2012): rows fill equal-volume buckets of `bucket_volume` (a row crossing a boundary is split pro rata), and `VPIN = sum(abs(buy - sell)) / (buckets * bucket_volume)` over the last `buckets` completed buckets, with `buy - sell` = the bucket's signed volume.
returns: `DOUBLE` in [0, 1]; positional `buckets` (50) and required positive `bucket_volume` (for example daily volume / 50). `NULL` until `buckets` buckets complete. `signed_volume` is buy minus sell volume (for example from bulk volume classification or `fin_trade_sign`); a row with `abs(signed_volume) > volume` or negative volume makes the result `NULL`. 0.3.0 BREAKING: `bucket_volume` is required (calls without it raise an error) and the old net-imbalance ratio is gone. Recursive: depends on every row since the first row (or window frame start). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_vpin(signed_volume, volume, 5, 100.0 ORDER BY ts) AS vpin FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 50.0 AS volume, CASE WHEN i % 3 = 0 THEN -30.0 ELSE 20.0 END AS signed_volume FROM range(20) t(i));

name: fin_vwap
purpose: Volume-weighted average price `sum(price * volume) / sum(volume)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`. Order-independent native aggregate; runs over any window frame. Rows with a `NULL` price or volume are skipped; a non-finite input or a negative volume makes the group `NULL`; a zero total volume gives `NULL`. Compensated summation.
example: SELECT fin_vwap(price, volume) AS vwap FROM (VALUES (100.0, 200.0), (101.0, 100.0), (100.5, 300.0)) t(price, volume);

name: fin_weighted_close
purpose: Weighted close `(high + low + 2 * close) / 4` (TA-Lib `WCLPRICE`).
returns: `DOUBLE` scalar; `NULL` input or non-finite result gives `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_weighted_close(102.0, 99.0, 101.0) AS weighted_close;

name: fin_weighted_mean
purpose: Compute the mean over value/weight pairs.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. NULL pairs are skipped; non-finite values or weights, or negative weights, make the group `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_weighted_mean(x, w) AS weighted_mean FROM (VALUES (1.0, 1.0), (2.0, 2.0), (3.0, 1.0)) t(x, w);

name: fin_weighted_quantile
purpose: Compute a quantile from the weighted empirical distribution.
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `(x, w, q [, method])`. Interpolates between successive cumulative-weight knots (inverted weighted CDF), not unweighted `quantile_cont` positions: with equal weights `'linear'` differs from numpy's default (type 7) `linear`; use `quantile_cont` for unweighted data. Equal values use increasing-weight order to define interpolation knots. Supports `linear`, `lower`, `higher`, `nearest`, `midpoint`, and `inverted_cdf` case-insensitively; unknown methods raise an error. Zero weights and NULL rows are ignored; non-finite values or weights and negative weights make the group `NULL`. `q` must be in [0,1] and, with the method, constant within each group. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_weighted_quantile(x, w, 0.5, 'linear') AS weighted_median FROM (VALUES (1.0, 1.0), (2.0, 2.0), (3.0, 1.0)) t(x, w);

name: fin_weighted_stddev
purpose: Square root of `fin_weighted_var`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_weighted_stddev(x, w, 0) AS weighted_stddev FROM (VALUES (1.0, 1.0), (2.0, 2.0), (3.0, 1.0)) t(x, w);

name: fin_weighted_var
purpose: Compute weighted variance with denominator `sum(w) - ddof`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Returns `NULL` when the denominator is not positive, the accumulated moments overflow, or an input is non-finite or a weight is negative.
example: SELECT fin_weighted_var(x, w, 0) AS weighted_variance FROM (VALUES (1.0, 1.0), (2.0, 2.0), (3.0, 1.0)) t(x, w);

name: fin_welch_ttest
purpose: Welch's unequal-variance two-sample t test.
returns: `STRUCT(stat, pvalue, df)`; same as `fin_ttest_2samp(x, y, false)` with fractional Welch-Satterthwaite `df`.
example: SELECT fin_welch_ttest(x, y) AS welch FROM (VALUES (1.0, 2.0), (2.0, 3.0), (3.0, 6.5), (2.5, 3.5)) t(x, y);

name: fin_willr
usage: fin_willr(high, low, close, 14 ORDER BY ts)
purpose: Williams %R `-100 * (HH - close) / (HH - LL)` over the last `period` rows (TA-Lib `WILLR`).
returns: `DOUBLE` in [-100, 0]; default period 14. `NULL` for the first `period - 1` rows. A flat range gives 0 (TA-Lib). Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_willr(high, low, close, 14 ORDER BY ts) AS williams_r FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close, close + 1.5 AS high, close - 0.5 AS low FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_win_rate
purpose: Fraction of non-NULL observations above zero.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_win_rate(r) AS win_rate FROM (VALUES (0.02), (-0.01), (0.03), (-0.015)) t(r);

name: fin_winsorized_mean
purpose: Clamp observations to the lower and upper continuous quantiles, then average them.
returns: `DOUBLE`; positional `(x [, lower_q, upper_q])`, defaults 0.05 and 0.95; bounds must satisfy `0 <= lower_q <= upper_q <= 1`. Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`. Runs as a window function; framed values equal the grouped result over the frame rows.
example: SELECT fin_winsorized_mean(x, 0.1, 0.9) AS winsorized_mean FROM (VALUES (1.0), (2.0), (3.0), (4.0), (100.0)) t(x);

name: fin_wma
purpose: Linearly weighted moving average of the last `period` values, weights `1..period` with the newest row heaviest (TA-Lib `WMA`).
returns: `DOUBLE`; default period 20. `NULL` for the first `period - 1` rows. Order-dependent native aggregate: grouped calls need `ORDER BY` inside the call and return the value at the last row; a window with `ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` reproduces the TA-Lib series. See [technical indicator conventions](#technical-indicator-conventions).
example: SELECT fin_wma(close, 20 ORDER BY ts) AS wma FROM (SELECT i AS ts, 100 + 3 * sin(i / 4) + i / 10 AS close FROM range(60) t(i));

name: fin_xirr
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
purpose: Internal rate of return of dated cash flows: the annual rate where `sum(cf_i / (1 + r)^((d_i - d_0) / 365)) = 0`.
returns: Uses a 10% default guess and ACT/365F times; a supplied guess selects among multiple valid roots. Dates may be `DATE`, `TIMESTAMP`, or `TIMESTAMPTZ` lists. Normalizes cash-flow amounts before solving. Infinite dates or no root return `NULL`.

name: fin_yang_zhang_vol
usage: fin_yang_zhang_vol(open, high, low, close ORDER BY ts)
purpose: Yang-Zhang (2000) volatility: `sqrt(annualization * (var(o) + k var(c) + (1 - k) mean(rs)))` over periods 2..N, with overnight `o = ln(O_t / C_{t-1})`, open-close `c = ln(C_t / O_t)`, Rogers-Satchell `rs`, sample variances and `k = 0.34 / (1.34 + (n + 1) / (n - 1))`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; optional positional annualization (default 252). Needs at least three bars; invalid bars make the group `NULL`. 0.3.0 replaced the former Rogers-Satchell copy. Order-dependent native aggregate: pass `ORDER BY` inside the call or use a window `ORDER BY`; rows with equal ordering keys have unspecified relative order, so break ties in the key. Native aggregate: pass arguments by position or as `name := value`.

name: fin_yearfrac
category: Fixed Income, Rates, And Cash Flows
purpose: Compute a day-count year fraction between two dates.
returns: `DOUBLE`; conventions `ACT/365F` (default), `ACT/360`, `ACT/ACT` (ISDA), `30/360` (Bond Basis), `30U/360` (US/SIA, February end-of-month rules), and `30E/360`. Accepts `DATE`, `TIMESTAMP`, or `TIMESTAMPTZ` (the time is dropped; `TIMESTAMPTZ` converts in the session `TimeZone` and needs ICU). Reversed `ACT/ACT` dates return the negative forward fraction. Unknown conventions raise an error.
example: SELECT fin_yearfrac(DATE '2026-01-15', DATE '2026-07-15', '30/360') AS year_fraction;

name: fin_zscore_last
purpose: Z-score of the latest observation by `ts`: `(x_last - avg(x)) / stddev_samp(x)`.
returns: `DOUBLE`; SQL macro. Ties on `ts` pick the largest `x`; `ts` may be an integer, floating-point, `DATE`, `TIMESTAMP` or `TIMESTAMPTZ` column. 0.3.0 added the ordering argument (the order-less form used an arbitrary row). Non-finite input makes the group `NULL`.
example: SELECT fin_zscore_last(x, ts) AS zscore FROM (VALUES (1, 10.0), (2, 11.0), (3, 9.5), (4, 12.0)) t(ts, x);

name: fin_ztest_mean
purpose: One-sample z test of the mean.
returns: `STRUCT(stat, pvalue)` of DOUBLE; `z = (mean - mu) / (sigma / sqrt(n))` with two-sided normal p-value. `sigma` defaults to the sample standard deviation (then two rows are required); an explicit `sigma` must be positive. NaN/inf input returns `NULL`. 0.3.0 changed the return type from DOUBLE. SQL macro.
example: SELECT fin_ztest_mean(x, 0.0, 1.0) AS ztest FROM (VALUES (0.5), (1.2), (0.8), (1.5), (0.9)) t(x);
